## Round 51: beam ends and a critical visual pass (2026-11-12)

Not committed. No generator run. `ArtSource/` exports and `Tools/Blender/` untouched (the Blender agents' files in the tree
are theirs). Save `progress.json` **2eca347e** copied aside before every Play Mode run and verified after each.

New rule (Remco): no effect may start or end with a hard edge; every beam, trail, line and glow tapers, flares or fades at both
ends and joins its source.

### 1. Line ends (`Game.Core.LineKit`, every user)

- **Width curve:** `UseBeam` and the new `ShapeEnds` give every line and trail a curve that grows from 0 at the source and
  falls back to 0 at the far end, eased (`2s - s²`, no corner at full width). Trails: 12 % head, 45 % tail.
- **Lines are laid through the kit:** `LineKit.Straight(line, from, to)` and `LineKit.Curve(line, from, control, to)` (a
  quadratic Bézier) lay 32 points, 6 of them inside each taper. The tapers are sized from the line's width (1.2 widths at the
  source, 1.5 at the far end), not from its length. A line renderer samples its width only at its points, so the old
  two-point lines could not taper at all. No allocation per frame (one scratch curve, `FitEnds`).
- **Round caps** (6 vertices). **No corner vertices:** the line lab (`r51_line_lab.cs`) showed the corner fans of a wide strip
  sticking out as teeth where it bends.
- **Profile fades along its length:** `SpriteKit.Beam` fades in and out over the first and last 3 % of U (8 % at first; that
  left a visible gap between the hero's muzzle and his bolt).
- **Flares:** new `Game.Combat.BeamFlare`, a camera-facing card in `LineKit.Flare()` (`SpriteKit.Glow`: a Gaussian white-hot
  point in a Gaussian glow that is eased to nothing before the card's rim), sized from the beam's width.
- **Users:** boss beam and halo (`BossAbilityView`), projectile beams, arcs and trails including the painted ones and the smoke
  ribbon (`ProjectileView`; the jagged arc fits its tapers with `FitEnds`), hero bolt (`HeroArtView`, `BlasterRig`), repair beam
  (`HeroAbilityView`, now from the `Weapon_L` fist when the figure has it), sword trail (`SwordRig`), recon trails (both,
  `ReconView`), drone thruster trails (`DroneView`: `startWidth/endWidth` replaced by `widthMultiplier`, or the kit's curve
  was overwritten).

### 2. Ray boss beam

- The opaque emissive sphere at the beam's end (`BeamTip`, 0.5 across at emission 3) was the "huge white disc" on the gate in
  `r50_laser_fire_side.png`. It is gone; the beam now ends in a soft impact flare 1.4 halo widths across and starts in a source
  flare 0.8 halo widths across, centred on the socket point itself.
- The three-point bend is now the Bézier's control point: the beam leaves the spade along its axis and curves to the target.
  Two fixes after looking at 4x crops:
  - only the part of the spade's axis that crosses the screen is used (a lead towards the camera folded the start of the strip
    into a few pixels);
  - the lead fades out as the spade turns away from the target and is gone at 60 degrees or more (`MinLeadAlignment`): a
    hairpin folded the 0.95-wide halo over itself (seen in the line lab). `r51_beam_points.cs` now shows turns of 0-1 degree per
    point on screen.
- Seen in the stills, not changed: the boss is hit while firing, and the covering impact puffs (`Gameplay/Impact`) sometimes sit
  over the beam's start. When the harness forces a laser without the Release clip, the beam runs straight from the tail through
  the body (round 50 open point 2 still stands for that case).

## Round 53 (Unity): the Shattered's bar over its crest, PhaseBreak documented, the ruin gate's threshold (2026-11-12)

Not committed. No generator run; `ArtSource/` and `Tools/Blender/` untouched (the two Blender agents' exports not synced).
Save `progress.json` **2eca347e** copied to the scratchpad before each of the four Play Mode runs, restored and verified after.

### 1. The bar inside the crest (round 52 open point 1)

- **The diagnosis was a probe bug, not the clips.** In play the crystals stand at 0.25 like in the clips (no phase look runs
  before the rejoin), and the drawn top is **2.77**, 0.25 under the bar (3.02). `BakeMesh(useScale: true)` returns the
  renderer's *local* vertices; `position + rotation * v` drops the boss's 0.8 parent scale, so `r49s3_bar_probe.cs` (and
  round 52) read the top at its unscaled size (3.35..3.47). Proof: `r53_bake_scale.cs` (same pose at root scale 1 and 0.8:
  bounds 2.771, old formula 3.464). `CreatureBarHeight.BakedTop` now uses the renderer's whole matrix (no height changes:
  the builder measures at scale 1); `r49s3_bar_probe.cs`, `r49s3_height_scan.cs` fixed the same way.
- **The real read:** at 3x the shard spires still cross the bar when the giant walks towards or away from the camera
  (`r53_bar_0/180/walk` before the fix): the camera looks down 44 degrees, so a spire leaning away stands higher in the
  picture than its height. Side on (90) it was clear.
- **Fix (data-driven):** `BlenderArtEntry.BarCrestBones` names crown bones; `CreatureBarHeight` then measures those parts
  as the play camera projects them (height + depth away x tan 44) at four headings, covered share 0.75 as before
  (`PlayCameraPitchDegrees` = 44, a test keeps every level's camera on it). Shattered row: `Core_Air`, `Core_Road`,
  `Core_Land`. Height **3.464 -> 4.197** (bar 3.02 -> **3.61** world; written by `r53_remeasure.cs`, no rebuild; the next
  import writes the same through the builder).
- **Other phase-scaled bosses** (`r53_held_top.cs`): the Shattered's rejoined look (crystals 1.35, shells 0) changes the
  top by 0.001; the Frost Warden's rage icicles at full scale give 5.109 under its stored 5.134 (calm 0.2: 4.80). Both bars
  already are the max over their phase states.

## Round 53 (Blender): the RuinGate rebuilt as one arch, the Shattered's plates on their own bones (2026-11-12)

Blender only. Nothing under `Assets/` was touched, Unity was not run and nothing is committed. The Sealed One was not touched.

(gitignored).

### 1. RuinGate (`Tools/Blender/build_ruingate53.py`, new)

Remco: "this doesn't look right, that gate". The round-29 gate had several faults:
- It was built from eleven separate voussoir slabs with 7 cm gaps between them. Each slab had its own depth and width, which gave the
  hard steps and the seam at the keystone that showed light.
- The faces towards the opening had no light and read black.
- When opened, the iris petals stood in the opening: each swung 98 degrees back on its rim, and the floor petal lay in the threshold.
- The two buttress boulders with crystals stood apart from the pillars.

The new gate:
- **Arch:** one band of stone, swept from foot to foot. It has straight jambs and a pointed head made of two concentric arcs.
  - Its section is a rounded, chamfered rectangle. The wear and the chipped notches come from noise. The pillars flare and
    deepen towards their feet.
  - At the apex the band rises into a pointed crest, with three overcharged crystal horns rooted 0.45 m deep.
  - The joints are tight zig-zag hairline grooves that stay dark. The light comes only from three long cracks, a few small
    ones and the worn glyph bands, all in the Shattered's magenta-white.
- **Faces towards the opening:** paler stone, a glowing slot down the middle (the seat the seal withdraws into) and two rows
  of glyph dashes.
- **Side elements:** two stone roots per pillar grow out of the pillar's outer face and run down into the plinth. Crystal
  clusters break out of a pillar on each side and out of one shoulder, rooted 0.3 m inside the stone.
- **Plinth:** a worn, flat-topped dais (8.7 x 3.5 m, top 0.2 m). Its rounded rim meets the ground, and the seal sigil is
  carved into its top.
- **The seal (an aperture), after the curator's review of the first rise sheet:**
  - Five black-glass petals with hairline seams. The petals meet in the middle behind the knot, so there is no hole.
  - Rims: the petals' rims run 9 cm into the jambs, and the floor petal runs into the plinth.
  - Inside the iris the petals follow a blurred outline, so the pointed apex no longer creases them.
  - Edges: matte dark stone with a thin magenta rim (no pale grey).
  - On `Open`:
    - The knot flares (to 1.22), then collapses at 30-38 and draws its four shards in. Nothing flies, nothing is left behind.
    - Each petal folds as one solid piece along its rim's normal (non-uniform bone scale) onto a line through a pivot 0.3 m
      inside the stone. Its leading edge runs back to the rim, and it goes to nothing only once it lies flat inside the
      stone (k > 0.97).
    - The opening is convex, so that line stays in the stone along the whole rim.
    - The floor petal sinks into an organic groove across the threshold: a lens 3.7 m long that tapers to a point at
      both ends, with a wavering edge, a dark-violet floor and lit lips that fade with the taper (Remco's rule: no
      square-cut ends on the ground).
    - Order: bottom first, then alternating. The motion eases out: each petal folds quickly and seats slowly, so none
      lingers half-folded.
    - The seams no longer part at first light; the light is the rim glow.
  - In `Opened_Idle` the opening is clear.

Build notes:
- Each bone's parts are remeshed on their own (the arch, each petal, the knot, each seal shard), and every island is then
  made wholly one bone's. Specks under 8 vertices are dropped.
- The vertex AO and the map bake are done with the iris and seal lifted out of the way. Two earlier faults caused this:
  - the closed iris shaded the faces towards the opening;
  - the petal feet baked their outline into the threshold as dark dashes.
- The band is UV-cut by facet angle. As one closed piece, the minimum-stretch unwrap collapsed half of it.
- `build_bosses29_props.py --only RuinGate` now calls this builder; `--old-gate` still builds the round-29 gate.

**Unity contract (`RuinGateView`, `BlenderBossFxBuilder`):**
- Unchanged:
  - asset `RuinGate`, one material with 4 maps (1024, Low 512), 6400 tris;
  - bones Root, Seal, Seal_1..4, Petal_1..5 (Unity finds `Seal` for the shard burst);
  - clips Closed_Idle 72, Open 160, Opened_Idle 72;
  - Open moments: seal crack 30, first light 38, petals start 52, fully open 130;
  - pivot: the centre of the threshold on the ground, facing -Y in Blender, which is +Z in Unity.
- Changed:
  - the Petal bones are now scale-keyed (`scale_keyed_bones` gains Petal_1..5);
  - size 8.97 x 3.55 x 8.74 m (was 8.68 x 2.18 x 7.77);
  - opening 4.0 x 4.83 m (was 4.0 x 4.3).

**Checks:**

### 2. Shattered: each shell plate on its own bone (round 52, open point 2)

**Cause.** Round 49G remeshed all plates together. Touching plates welded into shared islands:
- Shell_1 with the Shell_5 pair;
- Shell_3/4 with the Shell_7 pair.

The purity pass then gave each merged island to whichever bone weighted it most, and that differed between LOD0 and LOD1.

**Fix** (`build_shattered2.separate_shell_fuse`):
- Each Shell bone's plates, spikes and straps are remeshed on their own.
- The purity pass picks an island's bone by the plate parts it was built from (nearest source surface, majority vote),
  not by its weights.
- Rebuilt with `build_shattered2.py` and then `build_shattered_mech.py --skip-shards`.

**Result:**
- **Islands per bone, identical in LOD0 and LOD1:** Shell_1, 2, 3, 4 and 8 carry one plate each, and Shell_5, 6 and 7 carry
  two (left and right). Every island is 100 % on its bone.
- New `Tools/Blender/r53_shell_throw.py` measures the exported FBX (`r53_shell_throw_after|before.json`):
  - PhaseBreak1 throws Shell_1..4 (frames 15-21) and keeps 5..7. Shell_8 also shows there because it rides the rearing
    head, not because it is thrown.
  - PhaseBreak2 throws Shell_5..8 (frames 17-21).
  - Split throws all eight.
  - Before, LOD1 threw the Shell_1 plate in PhaseBreak1 on Shell_5 and kept it, and the Shell_3/4 hump plates went with the
    Shell_7 flanks.
- The spikes on the middle of the hump plates are separate islands on their plate's bone (as before). LOD1's decimation
  splits one Shell_2 spike in two.
- **Strict floating check** (`--burst Split,Rejoin,PhaseBreak1,PhaseBreak2,Death`): **LOD0 0 / LOD1 0 floating outside burst
  clips** (burst_only 19 / 17).
- **Clip parity:** Shattered OK (`clip_parity_r53.json`). No bone, clip or event change.
- **Report:** tris 24087 / LOD1 9485 (was 24106 / 9483). The body and the detail maps were re-baked and the body UVs changed;
  the crystal maps are byte-identical.
- **Look:** unchanged. The same parts, palette and shapes; only the remesh grouping changed. Where two plates meet they now
  overlap instead of welding.
- **Loose sheets** `ArtSource/Previews/QA/r49g_shattered_r53_loose_<clip>.png`, all 15 clips. I looked at Walk, PhaseBreak1
  and PhaseBreak2: nothing hangs off the body, and the plates leave in the order above.
- No corrupted skin (the Shattered has none). Import: RebuildOnly **Shattered** (FBX, LOD1, report, all maps incl. `Low/`).
  The round-52 tests `ScaledOffParts_ArePureIslands_InBothRigs` should still pass.

## Round 52 SealedOne (Blender): concept B "The opening seal" built: one hooded head, one three-petal maw, a seal halo behind it (2026-11-12)

Blender only; nothing under `Assets/` touched, Unity not run, not committed. Backup of the export, the .blend and the
three scripts before this round: `ArtSource/Exports/_backup_r49/SealedOne_52/` (gitignored). Remco picked concept B of
round 49G ("continue with direction B ... it may be much more epic, as long as it's clear that there is a head").
Design reasoning: `ArtSource/DESIGN_NOTES.md`, "Round 52: the Sealed One, the opening seal".

### What it is now

- **One head**: a massive hood of near-black sealed stone (one shell of revolution with a crest and two cowl folds)
  sits on the hunched bone-stone body. Its face is a deep funnel ringed by a **gold seal collar** (two thin gold rings
  with a band of 14 seal glyphs). **Three pairs of small violet eyes** sit in dark sockets on the brow above it.
- **One mouth** (the face IS the mouth): three **bone-white petals** (upper right, upper left, lower) meet in a pointed
  snout. They hinge on the funnel lip and open outwards. At rest they stand 4 degrees apart: dark violet slits with
  teeth.
  - Inside: 47 matte-ivory teeth rooted in wet gums, in a row along both edges of every petal and in two inner rings
    round the funnel.
  - A hot violet gullet sits at the bottom of the funnel.
  - A **gold seal glyph on each petal's inner face** only shows as the maw opens. A faint carved version of the glyph
    is on each petal's outer face.
- **Halo behind the head, never in front of it**: three broken flat stone seal rings with gold glyphs on both faces.
  - Each ring sits on its own hub on an axle that grows out of the back of the hood, carried by stone tines, so a ring
    stays attached while it turns and flares.
  - Flares past 1.0 are halved (`RING_GROW`), so the halo stays clear of the back.
- **Framing shapes**:
  - two massive planted arms with dark stone shackles (gold glyph band) and broken three-link chain stubs;
  - three-fingered hands with talons;
  - dark stone mantles with the seal glyph on the shoulders;
  - a few violet crystals low on the back.

  The seven seal stones and the rubble ring are as before (shown in Rise only).
- **Removed**: the thin praying upper arms, which cluttered the front of the maw. Their bones `UArm_*` stay and are
  keyed, but deform nothing.
- Value plan from the play camera: dark hood, gold collar, pale snout, violet throat, mid-grey body.

### The maw is the mechanic (same bones, same clips)

The petals use the old face-plate rig: **`Plate_R` = upper right petal, `Plate_L` = upper left petal, `Jaw` = lower
petal**. Every clip that parted the plates now opens the maw: in `specs(plates=...)` each petal turns PETAL_K x plates
outwards about its hinge and never closes past rest.

### Round 52b: cracked stone arms with violet light (Remco's "Bijna": "the stone arms could use cracks with a purple glow")

Only the arms changed. Head, maw, halo, bones and clips are unchanged.

- **`build_sealedone.cracked(base, ...)`** wraps the stone styles of the upper arms, forearms, elbows, shoulders,
  stone mantles, hands and fingers. Its fracture field is shared in world space (`CRACK_SEEDS`), so cracks run on
  across the joins between parts. It adds:
  - **Deep fissures**: borders of a noise-warped Voronoi field (~0.5 m cells). They open and close along their length,
    so they branch and stop instead of drawing closed cells. Their width varies from 4 mm to 2.2 cm.
  - **Wider, hotter fissures near the elbows and shoulders.**
  - **Chipped edges**: pale fresh stone and small breaks along the open fissures.
  - **Hairlines** from a finer field: dark, dry cracks. They glow only where they branch off an open fissure.
- **Glow**: violet (the throat's colour), varying along each crack: 0.2 to 1.0 x in the fissures, about 0.4 x in the
  branches, near zero in the hairlines.
- **Old veins toned down**: the stone's own violet seams on the arm pillars are lowered (glow 0.15 -> 0.05) and the
  slab veins on shoulders and mantles likewise.
- **Glow brightening with the maw**: per clip it is not possible, because emission is constant per clip. But the crack
  light is violet, so the existing phase emission sets (`SealedOne_Phase2..4_Emission`, `_Release_Emission`, re-made
  from this bake) already lift it with the rest of the entity (gain 1.35 / 1.6 / 1.5 / 2.2, tinted). Release turns it
  white.
- **Rubble ring**: stones within 18-66 degrees of the front are left out. Two stones touched the fingers, fused into
  the hand and stayed visible in every clip once `split_rubble` no longer moved them.

**Unity import**: the same single row, SealedOne. Triangles 39350 / 15495 with parts (body 25501 + Seal 8986 / LOD1
14000). The body and Seal maps and all phase emission sets are re-baked; UVs changed. Bones, clips, events, sockets and
`ExtraParts` are unchanged.

**Checks after the re-bake**:
- Clip parity against 2e4fc688: **OK** (`Jaw` is the only new bone, as before).

  walks straight out along the gate's axis; the route already runs straight on for 3 cells (it never turns inside or beside

  the arrow), cyan = towards the play camera (74 degrees off the axis), white = the plinth's footprint.

### B. Motion polish

1. **Builders (opening cutscene)**: every leg now carries one yaw, unwrapped along the builder's whole flight once at plan
   time (`FieldBase.AssignYaws`: flight = its way, weld = facing its module, climb/drop/hold = the heading before, landed =
   facing the base, each the short way from the leg before). The window average uses `HeadingBlend.AddYaw` (new: an
   unwrapped yaw as given) with the plain triangle window weights; the round-48 speed weights are gone (they squeezed each
   turn into the few slow frames at a join). Deterministic from the shot time as before.
2. **Hauler rotors**: `CutsceneMath.SpinUp` (speed rising evenly from rest over `RotorSpinUpSeconds` 0.8 s) at lift-off; the
   errand drone runs at full speed from its shot's first frame.
3. **Hero repeated fire**: the Shoot clip's first frame is the aim and is now **held** (rate 0) instead of restarted per shot
   (its own kick snapped the arm 24 degrees in one frame and back); each shot lays a kick on the gun arm on top
   (`Game.Hero.RecoilKick`: `s^2 e^(2(1-s))`, peak 0.06 s, times the square of a smooth ramp over the bolt's 0.09 s life, so
   nothing on the shot frame and little while the bolt is lit; `RecoilDegrees` 16, the last 3 shots add up). The pistol draw
   is held on its last frame (identical to the aim, 0.0 degrees) and the aim takes over at full weight
   (`ModelClipPlayer.PlayUpper(..., carry: true)`), so the draw no longer fades to the legs' pose and back before the first
   shot.

## Round 58: Shattered Easy margin, the ray boss turns to its beam, the Sealed One's bar over its flare (2026-11-13)

### 1. Shattered on Easy back at x1.80

- No existing lever touched one boss on one difficulty (the boss share is per profile for every boss; the level's health
  multiplier and the arena waves are per level for every difficulty), so there is a new, data-driven one:
  **`BossDefinition._difficultyHealth`** (`BossDifficultyHealth`: profile name + factor, on top of the profile's boss share;
  not listed = 1; `OnValidate` flags empty names, factors <= 0 and doubles). Read by `EnemySpawner` (in play),
  `EnemyStats.HealthOn` / `DifficultyStats.ShareFor` (ledger, via `BalanceLedger.Stats`) and the finale probe's `ShareNow`.
  `InputHash` adds the factors only for a boss that has them (no calibration hash changes; the Shattered is in no campaign level).
- Generator: `BossSpec.DifficultyHealth`, the Shattered's `ShatteredEasyHealth` **1.3** (Easy only), written by
  `CreateBossData`; the asset set the same way by `Tools/PlayTest/r58_apply.cs` (no generator run).
- Why 1.3 and not the 9% the ratio suggests: x1.1 changed nothing (identical verdicts), x1.2 to x1.28 held x1.88, x1.3 holds
  x1.80 (`r58_finale_factors.sh`: four factors on w1..w4 at once). The probe's multiple scales the escorts too, the factor
  only the boss, so the boss alone has to carry the whole step. Easy's boss now carries a 0.8 x 1.3 = 1.04 share on 0.68
  health (absolute: 71% of Medium's).

| Finale probe, Shattered (`r55b_finale.sh`) | Easy | Medium | Hard | Psycho |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| round 55b, before the entrance move | x1.80 | x1.18 | x1.96 | x1.52 |
| round 58 before (entrance (34,21), re-run) | x1.96 | x1.18 | x1.96 | x1.52 |
| Easy factor 1.1 | x1.96 | x1.18 | x1.96 | x1.52 |
| **Easy factor 1.3 (applied)** | **x1.80** (1.80 won, 1.88 lost) | x1.18 | x1.96 | x1.52 |

Medium, Hard and Psycho: identical verdict sequences in every run.

### 2. The ray boss faces its target while it fires

- `BossAbilities.TryLaserAim(lead, out point)`: while the beam burns, its target; before, once a laser is due within the lead,
  the target it will lock onto (searched at most every 0.25 s, kept while in reach, measured flat like
  `StructureRegistry.FindNearest`). `Use` now fires at that kept target while it is in reach, else at the nearest as before,
  so the beam goes where the body turned.
- `EnemyView`: from the power clip's lead + `AimTurnLeadSeconds` 0.6 s (1.6 s before the shot with the Release clip) the
  body's yaw target is the aim point instead of the heading; `FacingEase.Step(..., AimTurnSeconds 0.25,
  AimTurnDegreesPerSecond 120)` (new capped overload) turns it, and the capped turn stays on for the way back to the road
  until within 2 degrees. Scripted mechanics still place the body exactly. `CreatureClips.LeadOf(slot)` gives the clip lead.
- Measured (`r58_laser_seq.sh` = r57's + `r58_aim_probe.cs` every 10 frames; `SIDE_OFFSET` places a probe tower beside the
  boss with `r58_side_tower.cs`): horizontal angle between the body's forward and the beam (socket to strike point) during
  the hold:

| Case | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| target straight ahead (the gate) | 0.2-3.4 deg | 0.1-4.6 deg |
| tower beside it (before 74 deg off its heading, after 72 deg) | **87-117 deg** | **0.7-13.5 deg** |
| tower behind-left (a 132 deg turn) | - | **0.2-9.2 deg** |

  The 132-degree turn runs at the cap (2.4 deg per frame), eases in over the last 25 degrees and is done 0.3 s before the
  shot; no frame turns faster than the cap. The residual 0-13 degrees is the tail swinging in the Release sustain loop (the
  socket moves, the body holds still). Beam start on `Emitter`: 0.000 in every sample. The first beam segment still leaves
  13-48 degrees off the body axis: the round-51 bend that starts the beam along the spade's own axis; the chord is on the axis.

### 3. The Sealed One's bar over its flared halo

- Chosen: **lift the bar while the clip plays**, measured per clip, instead of sampling the power clips into the one bar
  height. Sampling them would raise the bar over the whole walk by the flare (Summon's top 10.1 against the walk's 8.05 model
  units: 1.6 m higher all the time); per clip the bar stays snug over the walk and rises only while the clip plays.
- `ModelClip._barTops` (float[], one per camera heading round the model, 24 every 15 degrees; empty = no lift), `LiftsBar`,
  `BarTopAt(heading)`. Written by `BlenderArtBuilder.WriteBars` (also reachable through the new `RemeasureBars(ids)`, used
  here instead of a rebuild) for rows with crest bones, for the clips played in place in a fight
  (`CreatureBarHeight.FightsInPlace`: attack, power, roar, enrage, adapt, phase break, split, rejoin, smash, volley, eggs,
  freeze, armour break; not the hit flinch, not climbs, dives, burrows or the rise onto the base, and not the death clip, which
  plays on the corpse without a bar), from `CreatureBarHeight.ClipBars` (the highest of the clip's 16 samples per heading,
  crest projected as for the cycles). `EnemyView.LiftBar` eases the bar (0.12 s) to `BarTopAt(camera heading in the model's
  frame)` while such a clip is on top, and back after.
- Four headings were tried first and were too coarse: the halo stands highest between them (Adapt 0.6 above its nearest
  sample at 45 degrees) and in play the bar was still crossed by 12 px at the moment. With 24 headings, written = measured
  (`r58_heading_tops.cs`).
- Lifts written: SealedOne Summon (10.10 with the camera on its far side, 7.04 the other way), Roar (9.97), Adapt (9.49 at
  45 deg); the Shattered (the other crest row, same bug) Roar 5.83, Split 5.02, Rejoin 4.43, PhaseBreak1/2 4.32 (bar 4.197).
  No other creature's bar moves; the walk bars are unchanged (8.054, 4.197).
- In play (`r58_summon.sh` + `r58_bar_probe.cs`, Level_C1_01, the Sealed One walking across the camera, 1920x1080 framing):
  walking, the bar's plate clears the halo by 74-87 px; through Summon the bar rises from 6.69 to 8.27 m and the plate clears
  the halo by **3-58 px (minimum 3 px at the moment, t 1.40-1.50 s)**, where the walk bar would be **crossed by up to 85 px**.
  Roar and Adapt were not played in Play Mode (offline measure only).
- Stills: `r58_SealedOne_summon` (+ `_game`; play camera, not orbited, t 1.64 s), crops `r58_SealedOne_summon_bar_x3` (+
  `_game_`): the bar and its armour line stand clear above the halo's top rings with a small gap.

## Round 61: air needs the sky gun, and a shockwave worth looking at (2026-11-13)

Not committed (the curator commits). No full generator run: `Tools/PlayTest/Scripts/ApplyRound61.cs` (the Gun Turret's air share,
the shockwave asset on the effect library) and the solve stage (`ApplyWaves.cs`) write what the changed generator now would.
`ArtSource/Exports` and `Tools/Blender` untouched, no Blender, no packages, the Game view's resolution untouched. Remco's save
`progress.json` (MD5 **10522349c3c6ea16ba72897a65724cff** at the start) was copied aside before every Play Mode run and restored
after; verified identical after each run and at the end; the dev backup untouched. Play runs strictly one after another.

### 1. "You don't need air defence on Easy"

**Diagnosis** (`AirDefenceProbeTests`, the ledger bot three ways, seeds 1-3; `Tools/PlayTest/r61_air_defence_before.txt`). Towers
that hit air: Gun Turret (ground and air, half damage up there), Flak (air only), the base's own turret; the hero's blaster and the
attack drone also reach up. Cannon and Laser do not.

| Before (seeds 1-3) | no sky gun | two Flaks | who took the flyers' health |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shard Ridge Easy | won 3/3, base 700/700, 11/11 flyers down, 0 base hits | identical | Gun Turret **100 %** without Flak; with it Flak 68-75 %, Gun 25-32 % |
| Fault Line Easy | won 3/3, base 700/700, all flyers down | identical | Gun Turret **91-93 %** (the rest unattributed, most likely the hero); with Flak 58-65 % Flak |
| Shard Ridge Medium | lost 3/3 at wave 14 (4/9 down, 117 base hits) | won 3/3, base 658-682 | Flak 90-100 % |
| Fault Line Medium | lost 3/3 at wave 16 | won 3/3, base 670-700 | Flak 55-65 %, Gun 25-35 % |

So Medium already needed the Flak; Easy never did. The sky per wave (`Tools/PlayTest/r61_air_waves.cs`): Shard Ridge Easy had two
raids, **four Skyrays of 8 health and seven of 25** (205 health in the whole level, 3.8 % of it); Medium's first raid was four
Skyrays of 18. The cause is in the paper, not in a number someone typed: the ledger buys a gun that only aims up while the flyers'
pressure is above one, the solver aims a raid at 0.3-0.8, so the ledger held every small raid with a row of Gun Turrets (thirteen
of them on Shard Ridge Easy wave 12) and the solver sized the raid against that row. Details in Docs/BALANCE.md "Air needs the sky gun".

**Fix** (the lever is on the cause; a flyer-health or count tweak per level would have been undone by the next solve):

| Lever | Before | After | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Gun Turret air share (`TowerDefinition._airDamageFactor`, `ProjectGenerator.GunAirShare`) | 0.5 | **0.2** | the generalist stops doing the Flak's job; the same share light fire has against armour |
| `BalanceRules.SkyGunForFlyers` (`Ledger.StandSkyGun`) | - | on | the expected player stands a sky gun for the first flyers, so raids are sized against it |
| `BalanceRules.RaidHealthFloor` (Easy / Medium / Hard / Psycho) | - | **0.6** / 0 / 0 / 0 | Easy's low pressure times the paper's low opinion of a Flak left raids no Flak was needed for; held inside the trim, so the level stays on its curve |
| `wave_tuning.txt` C1_06 Psycho | 0.57 | 0.52 | the trim could not land between 0.54 and 0.6 (a purchase flip: 1.20x against the curve's 1.31x, the band test failed); 0.52 is on the curve and keeps the level's total health within 2 % of the stored set |

The first two are a data number and a model rule; the rule is code under `Scripts/Balance` (the brief asked for data: the data
lever alone made the dead-zone raids smaller, see the lab table in BALANCE). C1_01 and C1_02 have no flyers on any difficulty and
are byte-identical (the lab: 0 waves moved). The waves of C1_03-C1_06 are re-solved on every difficulty. Raids after (flyers x
health each):

| Raids | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shard Ridge Easy | w12 4 x 8, w15 7 x 25 (level 205) | w12 4 x 33, w15 7 x 33 (level 359) |
| Shard Ridge Medium | w11 4 x 18, w12 5 x 116, w15 9 x 110 | w11 4 x 112, w12 5 x 108, w15 9 x 103 |
| Fault Line Easy | w10 2 x 45, w13 3 x 88, w16 3 + boss | w10 2 x 34, w13 3 x 72, w16 3 + boss |
| Fault Line Medium | w3 1 x 34, w6 1 x 34, w9 2 x 113, w12 3 x 141, w15 5 x 199 | w3 1 x 36, w6 1 x 51, w9 2 x 170, w12 3 x 149, w15 5 x 190 |

Paper side effects worth knowing: the ledger now pays for a Flak from the first flyers on, so the ground of the levels with early
flyers is trimmed lighter to stay on the curve (total health Fault Line Easy 7394 -> 5111, Hard 30607 -> 23321; Shard Ridge Easy
5325 -> 4971, Fault Line Medium 17385 -> 15991; C1_05 within 4 %, C1_06 Easy -11 %, Medium +7 %, Hard and Psycho within 2 %).

**Verify** (`r61_air_probe.sh`; Easy on the final waves `r61_air_defence_after_easy.txt`, Medium `r61_air_defence_after.txt`):

| After (seeds 1-3) | no sky gun | no sky gun, guns put beside the besieged base | two Flaks before the first raid |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shard Ridge Easy | **lost 3/3** at wave 14 (2/4 flyers down) | won 3/3, **1 star, base 158-273/700**, 96-116 base hits | won 3/3, 3 stars, 700/700, Flak takes about 90 % |
| Fault Line Easy | lost 1/3, won 2/3 at 700/700 | won 3/3 (base 465, 700, 700) | won 3/3, 3 stars, 700/700 |
| Shard Ridge Medium | lost 3/3 at wave 13 (0/9 down) | lost 3/3 | won 3/3, 3 stars, base 682-700 |
| Fault Line Medium | lost 3/3 at wave 12-13 | lost 3/3 at 13-16 | won 3/3: base **39** (1 star), 681, 700 |

Read: with the Flak the first air levels are clean on Easy and Medium; without it Shard Ridge Easy costs the base two thirds of its
health if the player patches with Gun Turrets, and the level if he does nothing. Flyers that reach the base stay and hit it until
something kills them, so "a leak" is never a few points: that is why the patching bot exists (`ProbeStrategy.NoSkyGunGuardsBase`).

### 2. The shockwave

It is the hero's first ability. It was a flat translucent cylinder that grew to the radius in 0.45 s (hard rim, cut by the gate)
plus a ring of 36 dust puffs. Now `ShockwaveView` plays a `ShockwaveVfxDefinition` (`Data/Vfx/Vfx_HeroShockwave.asset`, hung on
the `VfxLibrary`; generator spec `ShockwaveSpec` in `ProjectGenerator.Vfx.cs`): the painted ring card (bright edge, soft inner
falloff) racing to the ability's radius in 0.5 s with a cubic ease-out, an echo ring 0.13 s behind it at half strength, a pool of
light on the ground, the refraction ring (high profile only), an additive flash and a point light at the fist (0.35 s), 40 spark
streaks skimming outward, 18 glowing shards and 14 unlit dust puffs rolling out behind the front. It leaves 0.1 s after the request,
with the fist (`HeroArtView.AbilityLeadSeconds`). Colour: the ability's tint (cyan) lifted 35 % to white, blue-grey dust. Every
ring fades in over 8 % of its run and out from 40 % (smoothstep both ways), tested. Low profile: half the particles, no refraction,
no light. Build-safe: `VfxParticles` sheets, `ParticleKit` smoke, `GlowDecal`; no URP default material (tested). Without the
library's art the old plain ring and dust still play.

Stills (`ArtSource/Previews/QA/r61_shockwave_*`, the game's own light, 1920x1080, stepped frames of 0.02 s; `tNN` is the frame after
the request): `before_t04|t08|t13|t27` + `before_disc_x3`; `after_t06..t60` + `after_sheet`, crops `after_start_x3`, `after_core_x3`,
`after_rings_x2`, `after_end_x2`; `after_cannon_t08|t15` + `after_cannon_sheet` + `after_cannon_blast_x3` (a Cannon shell bursting
in the same frame); `low_t15|t20` + `low_sheet` + `low_core_x3`. What I see: the wave now holds its own next to the Cannon's
fireball instead of reading as a UI disc; the start grows out of the fist's flash and the end thins to nothing, no hard edge in the
x2/x3 crops. What is still weak: the rings read white-blue rather than clearly cyan; the sparks are short even dashes of one length;
the dust is grainy at x3; the refraction ring is not in these stills (the off-screen render has no opaque texture), so it was only
confirmed as switched on (`r61_shock_probe.cs`), not judged by eye; the before stills have no tower shot in frame (the walkers did
not reach the post in that run). The cannon stills are from the second tuning pass (dust and shards were made visible after it).

runs, 15 min 40 s) -> fit -> search (4 clones, 1.5 min) -> replay (198 runs, 21 min) -> fit on all records -> three cells one
builder step easier, solve, their measure/search/replay again -> fit -> `apply-keep` -> acceptance -> readme -> the suite.

**The calibration is current again (inputs 22954ca8) and `PlanSearchTests.Search_WritesPlansForEveryCell` passes instead of
skipping; its efficiencies were kept, not replaced.** The new fit (747 runs) reads Cannon 0.877 (+3 %), Laser 0.732 (-4 %), Gun
Turret 1.013 (+15 %), Flak 1.113 (+7 %) against the applied 0.853 / 0.759 / 0.878 / 1.041, hold-out 78 % / mono 88 % /

factors, the armoured troops, the wisp voices, the music import) and the solve stage (`ApplyWaves.cs`) write what the changed
generator now would. `ArtSource/Exports` and `Tools/Blender` untouched, no Blender, no packages, the Game view's resolution
untouched. Remco's save `progress.json` (MD5 **463303aa28769c0934c10dc303967162** at the start) was copied aside before every
Play Mode run in the editor and restored after; identical after each run and at the end (`Tools/PlayTest/r64_save_md5.txt`);
the dev backup untouched. Editor play runs strictly one after another, each harness waiting on the one before; the pipeline's
PlayMode stages on the five worker clones (w1-w5), EditMode on the spare clone w6. Tables and the model: Docs/BALANCE.md
"Round 64"; commands: Docs/COMMANDS.md "Round 64".

### 1. The loading screen (`Game.UI.LevelLoader`, `LoadingScreen`, `LoadingProgress`, `LoadingTips`, `LoadingArt`, `ILevelLoadProgress`)

**The freeze, measured** (`r64_hitch.sh`, Shard Ridge on Easy from the menu, real time per frame): choosing a difficulty loaded
the Level scene and built the whole level in **one frame of 3165 ms**. Where it went (stopwatch marks in the bootstrapper):
1.6 s decoding the two music loops whole the first time they played (30 MB of Vorbis each, "decompress on load"), 0.7 s
synthesising the generated score and some forty generated sound effects that are then never played because the recordings
exist, 0.5 s the terrain field, 0.3 s the props, 0.2 s each for the surface, the gates and the HUD.

**What changed.**
- Every way into a level that is not a cut of its own (the map, "Play again", the pause menu's restart, a practice fight)
  goes through `LevelLoader`: the screen fades in over 0.3 s, the scene is loaded in the background once the screen covers
  everything, the level is built **a step a frame** behind it (`LevelBootstrapper.Build`, `LevelVisualBuilder.BuildInSteps`:
  setup, terrain field, surface, liquids, props, environment kit, mist, markers, origins, sound, gameplay; each reports its
  share), and the screen fades out over 0.45 s once the bar is full and four frames in a row ran under 50 ms (at most 2 s).
  No hard cut either way; a long frame cannot turn a fade into a cut (the fade moves at most 1/30 s a frame). A level loaded
  directly (tests, probes, the cutscene's handoff) is built in one frame as before.
- The waste is gone rather than hidden: the music loops **stream** (`ProjectGenerator.ApplyMusicImport`; also the menu's loop),
  the generated fallbacks are only synthesised when a recording is missing (`SoundFamily(set, Func<AudioClip>)`,
  `MusicPlayer.Recorded`), and the generated ambience bed is made on a step of its own.
- The look: the menu's painted night sky, the planet's limb painted in code from the level's `VisualTheme` (ground and accent
  colours, a night side, a rim of air) with two scan rings turning round it, "DEPLOYING TO", the level's name, its continent
  and the difficulty, one line of Dr. Voss's advice and a thin bar with a light riding its end and a percentage. The advice is
  the closing line of the story's own scan hints and gate tips (`LoadingTips`, no new copy); hints about creatures the level
  sends on that difficulty come first and the screen opens on one of those; a new line fades in every 5.5 s.
- Nothing on it can be pressed, so it needs no focus: it swallows clicks, drops the focus of the button that started the load
  (a second Confirm cannot start it twice; `LevelLoader.Busy`), and runs on unscaled time. It uses the game's scaled canvas
  and safe frame, with 96 px of its own at the sides (the safe frame adds nothing on a monitor).

**Measured after** (the same run, `Logs/r64/hitch_after_c103_easy.txt`; in the editor with the tools attached, so a build is
faster on both sides):

| Shard Ridge, Easy, from the menu | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Longest frame | **3165 ms** (the whole load, the map frozen) | **798 ms** (the gameplay step, behind the screen; 606 ms in an earlier run) |
| Frames over 50 ms | 1 | 11: the click 85 + 111 ms, the scene 70, terrain field 510, surface 209, liquids 115, props 304, kit 154, sound 70, gameplay 798, first level frame 57 |
| Level ready after the click | 3.17 s (nothing on screen moves) | 2.76 s (0.3 s of it the fade in) |
| Loading screen gone | - | 3.33 s |

Honest reading: the freeze became a loading screen, and the load itself is a little shorter, but the screen is not smooth all
the way: the terrain field (0.5 s) and the gameplay step (0.6-0.8 s: gates and base turrets 0.2, sounds 0.15, HUD 0.14) are
still single frames in which the rings and the bar stand still. The bar itself eases, so it never jumps, and fills at once
when the load is done. Cutting those two steps further means building the gameplay over several frames, which changes the
order things wake up in; not done in this round.

Stills (`ArtSource/Previews/QA/`, rendered off-screen with the interface at 1920x1080, `_720` at 1280x720; stepped frames):
`r64_loading_1_fade_in` (+`_x2`: the map under the screen at 18 %), `_2_covered`, `_3_mid` (+`_720`, `_title_x2`, `_tip_x2`,
`_bar_x2`, `_planet_x2`), `_4_late` (100 %, the next tip), `_5_after` (the level, the screen gone). What I see in the x2
crops: the title and the tip are clean and as readable at 720p as at 1080p; the bar starts and ends in a soft light (its
square start in the first pass is gone); the planet's limb is clean and nothing ends on a hard edge. Weak: the planet is
soft (384 px drawn at 980) and its cloud bands are low in contrast, grey-violet on Shard Ridge's palette, so it reads as
"a planet" more than as this level's place; the rings are faint; the small labels are 19 px at 720p.

### 2. The field stops when the level is over (`ResultView.Freeze`)

The result panel reset the clock to normal speed and the level played on behind it. Now the clock winds down to zero over
0.5 s (real time, smoothstep) the moment the panel appears, on a win and on a defeat: creatures, towers, shots, drones,
particles and every timer run on game time, so they all stop; the panel, its stars and its buttons run on unscaled time as
before. The defeat keeps its 3.2 s of the base going up before the panel, and a victory dialogue or a boss's end still
plays first. "Play again" and the pause menu's restart leave the clock stopped under the loading screen; the loader starts
it for the new level. The level's running sounds already fell silent at the outcome (`SfxPlayer`) and the ambience fades
out (`MusicPlayer`); the score plays on over the panel as it did.

Measured (`r64_gameover.sh`, Shard Ridge Hard, a defeat; `r64_gameover.cs probe` 1.5, 5.5 and 8.5 s after): time scale
**0.000**, game time **91.846** on all three, the summed positions of the 22 living creatures, the shots and the drones
identical to four decimals on all three, the panel up, the only loop still audible the score (0.28). The two stills taken
3 s apart differ in 0.45 % of their pixels (the focus frame's pulse and the radar, both interface).

### 4. Armour across all weapons

**Found** (`ArmourTtk.cs`, every damage source against every armoured troop through the game's own `Health`):
- **The attack drone had no armour factor.** Its shots went through the projectile pool at the default of one, like a shell:
  a Cragback in 18.5 s where the rule would give 38 s. Mines, the barrel, the lava ball and the ground drone were the same
  (meant as heavy, but never data).
- **The Laser never bypassed armour; the armour was too small to matter.** The pool is spent point for point, so a beam of
  small ticks pays what one big hit pays (no per-tick loophole, no damage-over-time path round it). But a Cragback was 160
  body + 60 armour: light fire paid 2.1 times what a shell paid, and the Laser has 2.6 times the Cannon's damage per second per
  coin. Per coin the Laser killed a Cragback as fast as the Cannon did. Armour forced nothing.

**The rule** (one table, data): every weapon has a `DamageType`; what neither explodes nor pierces is reduced by armour.
Bullet and Beam 0.2 (Gun Turret, base turret, gate gun, blaster, **attack drone**, Laser, Cryo), Blade, Arc, Burn and Ram 0.5
(**energy sword, was 1**; Tesla; **lava ball and ground drone, were 1**), Explosive 1 (Cannon, Artillery, mine, barrel,
shockwave, **Flak, was 0.5**: its shells burst, and no armoured flyer exists), Piercing 1.5 (Railgun).
`BalanceSheet.ArmourFactorOf`, `ProjectGenerator.WeaponDamageTypes`, checked on every asset (`Round64Tests`, `OnValidate`).

**The armoured troops are mostly armour** (`BalanceSheet.TroopArmourShare` 0.72; the toughness a shell must deal is
unchanged): Cragback 160+60 -> **60+160**, Stinger 80+210, Shardback 90+240, Bulwark 155+405.

Seconds for one source to kill one Cragback at wave multiplier one (coins x seconds / 1000):

| Source | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gun Turret L1 / L3 | 32.2 s (1.6) / 7.8 s | **60.2 s (3.0)** / 14.5 s |
| Laser L1 / L3 | 11.6 s (1.5) / 3.9 s | **21.6 s (2.8)** / 7.2 s |
| Cannon L1 / L3 | 14.4 s (1.4) / 3.5 s | 14.4 s (1.4) / 3.5 s |
| Base turret L1 | 26.4 s | 49.2 s |
| Hero blade / blaster | 9.1 s / 23.2 s | 15.4 s / 43.0 s |
| Attack drone | 18.5 s (3.3) | **72.0 s (13.0)** |
| Mine (one blast) | 64 % of it | 64 % of it |
| Lava ball / ground drone (while touching) | 4.0 s / 7.4 s | 7.0 s / 12.7 s |

Against the other armoured species the ratios are the same (the full tables: `Tools/PlayTest/r64_armour_ttk_before.txt`,
`_after.txt`). Per coin a Laser or a Gun Turret needs twice what a Cannon needs for a Cragback (it was 1.05x and 1.14x),
and the Cannon's blast takes three at once; light fire still kills one alone and lands in full once the shells have
stripped the armour. In play the yardstick shows it: on Landing Site Hard the Gun Turret row won 3/3 and now loses 0/3 at
the last wave, the Cannon row went from 1/3 to 3/3.

### 5. Shard Ridge's bosses on Hard

**Cause.** A boss wave had one health multiplier for the boss and its crowd, the solver and the cap sized it by the crowd,
and the per-difficulty boss share (`DifficultyProfile.BossHealthShare`, round 10; it works as written) only ever applied
to continent bosses. On a crowded last wave the level's boss came out at a third of its book health: the Brood Mother of
Shard Ridge Hard had 900 x 0.337 x 1.15 = **349** hit points (Medium 327, Easy 122), the Core Wisp before it 565; Fault
Line Hard 279 and 217. Not round 62's builder step (Psycho only), not the armour bug (these bosses wear none).

**Fix.** A level's boss carries its own health scale on top of its wave's multiplier (`WaveDefinition._bossHealthScale`),
set by the solve (`CampaignModel.SizeBosses`): never under a floor (`LevelBossHealthFloor` 0.5 / 0.75 / 0.9 / 0.9 of its
book health), grown with the player's firepower until the boss alone asks `LevelBossAlone` (0.2 / 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.45 of
what the expected player with the hero can deal in its walk), but only as far as its wave still fits
`LevelBossGrowthCap` (1 / 1 / 1.15 / 1; set by the replays, see 6); a crowd gives way to a boss that pushed its wave over the hero cap.

hit points are nine seconds of fire instead of three; with a full defence it will still fall on the first stretch. I did
not run a boss-fight probe that measures where it dies. Making it more needs a thinner crowd on boss waves (tried on paper:
`BossWaveShare` 0.6 -> 0.3 gives 2150 there but 4500 for the mid-level Core Wisp of Crysium Vein Hard, so it needs a cap of
its own) or a boss that does more than walk. Also open: on Crysium Vein the Psycho last boss (1978) is now below Hard's
(2595), because Psycho bosses only grow while their wave is held.

### 6. The pipeline (all 24 cells)

Order as run: solve on the new mechanics -> measure (24 cells, 432 runs, 24 min) -> fit -> **apply (the new fit, not kept)**
-> solve -> search (6 levels on the clones, 4 min) -> replay (279 runs) -> acceptance -> three builder iterations on the
cells that fell (below) -> finale probe -> finale apply -> the suite.

**The calibration: the fit was applied.** The round re-solves every level anyway, so round 62's open question is moot. The
fit on the new yardstick (432 runs, no old replays): Cannon 0.853 -> **0.797**, Laser 0.759 -> **0.701**, Gun Turret 0.878 ->
**0.808**, Flak 1.041 -> **1.039**; route fire 4.0, queue guard 0.30, siege 1.187 -> 1.168; hold-out 81 % / mono 89 % /
Spearman 0.80 (below the 90 % bar as before, applied by override). The Gun Turret did not come out 15 % higher this time
but 8 % lower: round 62's reading leaned on replayed plans, and a later fit of this round with the 279 new replays in it
again reads Gun 0.871, Laser 0.741, route fire 2.0, queue guard 0.5. The fit still moves with the record set (a model
matter, as round 62 said); the applied one is the yardstick-only fit, kept through the later re-stamps
(`apply-keep`, calibration 2026-11-15 14:41, factors of 12:40 kept, inputs c0e168ae, current).

## Round 65: high ground (sloped plateaus, the line of fire, +10% range, Voss's hint), loading tips that stand alone, flyers that fly curves, bosses sized as a fight (2026-11-15)

Not committed (the curator commits). No full generator run: `Tools/PlayTest/Scripts/ApplyRound65.cs` (the terrain rules asset,
every level's plateaus and painted ground, the arena copies, the story's hints) and the solve stage (`ApplyWaves.cs`) write
what the changed generator now would. `ArtSource/Exports` and `Tools/Blender` untouched, no Blender, no packages, the Game
view's resolution untouched. Remco's save `progress.json` (MD5 **463303aa28769c0934c10dc303967162** at the start) was copied
aside before every Play Mode run in the editor and restored after; identical after each run and at the end; the dev backup
untouched. Editor play runs strictly one after another; the pipeline's PlayMode stages on the worker clones w1-w5, EditMode on
the spare clone w6. Tables and the model: Docs/BALANCE.md "Round 65"; commands: Docs/COMMANDS.md "Round 65".

### 1. Plateaus slope down, and a gun on one never fires through the ground

**What was wrong, in numbers.** Raised ground ended in a wall inside its own cells (0.55 high, `TerrainField.ConfineToCells`),
dressed with square terrace-step kit pieces, and it could stand right beside the road. A tower's shot flies from its muzzle
to the creature's feet, and the muzzles are low: Cannon 0.34 over its pad, Gun Turret 0.39, Railgun 0.42, Laser 0.48
(`Tools/PlayTest/r65_muzzles.cs`). From the second row of a plateau the line to a creature under the wall passed 0.1 to 0.2
under the lip, which is the Laser Remco saw.

**The rules now** (`Game.Levels.PlateauSkirt`, pure, on cells; one place the generator, the validator and the landscape share):
- Raised ground keeps **one cell clear** of everything that must stay level: the road, a liquid, a mining node, a nest, a boss
  gate's footprint. A raised cell touching one of those (eight ways) is taken down to plain ground.
- The **ring** of plain ground round what is left is the slope. It is data (`LevelDefinition._slopeCells`), no tower stands on
  it (`BuildGrid.IsSlope`; the placing status says "Too steep: the slope of the high ground holds no tower"), and the
  build-cell glow, the radar and the plan model's spots leave it out because they all ask `BuildGrid.CanBuild`.
- A raised cell whose straight line to some road cell in reach leaves the plateau later than **0.54 of the way** (the terrain
  rules' sight ratio) is **closed** as a blocked cell: there the shot would dip under the plateau's own lip. A cell with one
  raised cell between it and the ring still sees the road (1.5 of 2.8 cells, the nearest a walker comes), a cell with two
  does not (2.5 of 3.8).
- `LevelValidator.CheckPlateaus` checks all three on every level (the generator's layout step runs it too).

**The landscape** (`TerrainField`): the plateau's level top is the raised cells drawn in by 0.3 of a cell (which rounds every
outer corner by that much), and from there the ground falls on a smooth curve over 1.08 cells, so it has run out before the
cell beyond the ring (shoulder 0.3 + slope 0.78 + a wandering foot of 0.05; one soft pass takes the crease out of inside
corners). The plateau is **0.33 high** now (0.55 before): with muzzles this low a taller one cannot be seen over from its
own second row, whatever the slope (the sums are in Docs/BALANCE.md). The terrace-step kit is no longer placed
(`EnvironmentLayout`); the pieces stay in the set.

**How it reads without a wall** (the first stills showed a slope nobody could see): the bank wears the set's cliff rock
through the mesh's vertex colours (`TerrainSurfaceBuilder`, `EnvironmentGround.shader`: `EnvironmentSet.PlateauBank`), the
level top wears the second ground layer (`EnvironmentSplat`, `PlateauTop`), and the painter draws a bank that is pale at the
top and dark at its foot with a soft seam of the level's glow wandering round it (`TerrainPainter.ShadeCliff`; broken up, so
it is a vein in the rock and not a drawn outline). Voss's hint points at exactly that seam.

**Every level** (`ApplyRound65`; campaign levels, the four arena copies follow their source):

| Level | Raised cells before | after (taken down) | Slope cells | Closed by the sight rule | Raised build cells | Build cells before -> after | Spots within 2 of the road | of them high ground |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| C1_01 Landing Site | 17 | 12 (5) | 29 | 1 | 11 | 450 -> 420 | 348 -> 333 | 11 -> 6 |
| C1_02 Glass Meadows | 26 | 13 (13) | 37 | 7 | 6 | 559 -> 515 | 335 -> 308 | 17 -> 3 |
| C1_03 Shard Ridge | 24 | 11 (13) | 38 | 2 | 9 | 534 -> 495 | 387 -> 348 | 24 -> 9 |
| C1_04 Fault Line | 15 | 12 (3) | 19 | 7 | 5 | 521 -> 495 | 432 -> 416 | 8 -> 3 |
| C1_05 Quartz Flats | 25 | 16 (9) | 31 | 0 | 16 | 570 -> 540 | 373 -> 361 | 5 -> 4 |

**The line-of-fire check** (`LineOfFireTests`, EditMode, in the suite): on every level, for every tower the level sells
against the ground at every upgrade level, from every raised build cell, the straight line from its lowest muzzle (the
imported model's shot origin at rest, over the cell's middle) to every point of the road a walker can be on within its reach
(the +10% included) is walked in steps of 0.05 against the drawn landscape. **127 244 lines, none under the ground**
(tolerance 0.01); the report is `Tools/PlayTest/r65_line_of_fire.txt`.

### 2. Ten percent more range on high ground

One number, in data: `Data/Balance/TerrainRules.asset` (`TerrainRules.HighGroundRange` 1.1; the generator's constant is
`ProjectGenerator.HighGroundRange`), and every level points at that one asset. Everything asks the same place
(`TerrainBalance.RangeMultiplier(level, cell)`):
- the tower itself (`Tower.GroundRange`, set when it is stood on its cell; `Tower.Range` and a support tower's radius carry
  it), so targeting reaches further for real;
- the **range ring**: the ring of a placed tower is its own range, the ring of the tower in hand grows on a raised cell;
- the **status line** while placing ("Cannon (100)  -  Ground only  -  High ground: +10% range") and the **tower menu's info
  line** ("Laser Turret  MAX  HP 160/160  -  Ground only  -  High ground: +10% range");
- the **balance model**: `BalanceLedger.Geometry` gives every raised spot the multiplier (`LevelGeometry.SpotRange`, the hook
  round 22 left for this), so the spot lens, the plan search and the input hash see it. The wave solve itself buys guns at
  the defence gate and did not move for it (see 5).

Measured in play: a Laser at level 3 on Landing Site's plateau reaches 5.28 (4.80 on the plain), a Cannon 4.40 (4.00).

### 3. Dr. Voss on high ground, and loading tips that stand on their own

**The hint** (`Dlg_Tip_HighGround`, `StoryDefinition.HighGroundTip`, three lines by Voss, proposed copy): it plays once per
save, right after the player has built a first tower in a level that has a raised build cell (`LevelStoryListener.WatchHighGround`,
`PlateauSkirt.HasBuildSpot`), through the same queue, hold and seen-flag as the gate tips. Landing Site has eleven such
cells, so a new player gets it in the first minute, when the second tower can use it. The ten percent in his line is written
from the generator's number.

> "Good, the first turret stands. Now look for the rises: ground with a glowing seam round its bank."
> "That is high ground. A turret on top of it sees further: 10% more range. The range ring shows it before you build."
> "The bank itself is too steep for a turret, so only the top counts. Take it where the road passes close."

**The loading tips.** The screen showed the closing line of each hint's conversation, which leans on the lines before it
("Ground guns can't touch it."). Every hint now carries its advice once more as a line written for the loading screen
(`DialogueDefinition.LoadingTip`, the table `ProjectGenerator.LoadingTipTexts`), naming the creature or the thing it is about,
and `LoadingTips` shows only those: twelve tips (eight creatures, the two gate tips, high ground, the rift behind the gates).
The Skyray's is now "Skyrays never land, so ground guns can't touch them. Build a Flak Turret where they cross the gates."
A test holds every creature tip to its creature's name and every tip to its box (150 characters).

### 4. Flyers fly curves and bank

**Where the sharp turns were.** The six levels' own flight routes have three waypoints and turn 1 to 47 degrees; the
right angles were flown by the **bats out of the nests**, which fly to the road and then along it, corner by corner, and by
every flyer that **dives at a gate** (the gate was a waypoint inserted into its route).

**Now** (`Game.Levels.FlightCurve`, pure; `EnemySpawner.FlightRoute`): when a flyer is launched, every corner of its route is
replaced by an arc. The radius is the creature's speed over its turn rate (`EnemyDefinition.TurnRate`, 60 degrees a second by
default, so a Skyray or a Shalebat at 1.3 turns on 1.24 cells, a Storm Matriarch on 1.05; never under 0.75 of a cell), drawn in
where a leg is too short for it. A flyer that strikes a gate swings past it on an arc too, as long as the arc still brings it
within 0.6 of its attack range of the gate (it stops there to strike, as before); a dive too sharp for that keeps its point.
The body **banks**: `EnemyView.Bank` rolls it into the turn by how fast its facing comes round, up to
`EnemyDefinition.BankDegrees` (28) at the full turn rate, eased over 0.3 s.

**Path lengths** (`Tools/PlayTest/r65_air_routes.txt`; cells):

| C1_02 north / south route | 37.19 / 44.01 | no flyers on this level | - | 4 / 43 deg |
| C1_03 north / south route (Skyray) | 41.85 / 37.53 | 41.85 / 37.52 | 0.0 % | 24 -> 8 / 19 -> 10 deg |
| C1_04 north / south route | 42.47 / 37.02 | 42.45 / 37.01 | 0.0 % | 28 -> 9 / 13 -> 7 deg |
| C1_05 north / south route | 47.48 / 39.03 | 47.42 / 39.03 | -0.1 % / 0 | 47 -> 12 / 1 deg |

| C1_04 nest flights (Shalebat, three nests) | 73.50 / 68.50 / 60.50 | 71.78 / 66.89 / 58.89 | -2.3 / -2.3 / -2.7 % | 90 -> 11 deg |
| C1_05 nest flights (two nests) | 105.50 / 61.50 | 100.14 / 58.28 | -5.1 / -5.2 % | 90 -> 11 deg |

The raid routes are as long as they were, so the raids' timing is unchanged; a bat out of a nest arrives 2 to 5 % sooner.
The balance model's air-route lengths were **not** changed: the model walks nest creatures along the road as written, and
2 to 5 % on the bats is far inside what the calibration resolves (its hold-out is 81 %). The routes are the same data, so
the validator's route checks are untouched; a test rounds every flight of every level for every flyer and holds it to its
route's own bounds, to at most 13 degrees between two points and to at most a tenth shorter.

In play (`Logs/r65/fly_trace.csv`, Fault Line, a Shalebat out of a nest and a Skyray on the north route, sampled every 0.2 s
of game time): the heading never changed more than 11.3 degrees between two samples (57 degrees a second, under the 60 it
may), and the bodies rolled up to 29 and 26.5 degrees in the turns (the bank plus the flight's own sway) and flew level between them.

### 5. The balance pass

Order as run: solve on the new maps -> a first full pass with a boss rule for every cell (measure 432 runs, fit,
apply-keep, search, replay 306 runs, acceptance), **taken back** (below) -> the per-cell lever -> solve -> measure (24 cells,
432 runs) -> fit -> **apply-keep** (the factors of round 64 stay: Cannon 0.797, Laser 0.701, Gun Turret 0.808, Flak 1.039; this
round's fit on the yardstick reads 0.794 / 0.686 / 0.848 / 0.982, hold-out 81 % / mono 87 % / Spearman 0.80, below the bar as
before) -> search (six levels on the six clones) -> replay -> acceptance.

**What the maps did to the waves: almost nothing.** With the plateau rules and the ten percent alone, the solve gave back
the stored waves of five levels exactly (0 waves moved); Landing Site moved by under 1.5 % of its total health. The wave
solve buys at the defence gate and does not read single spots. The plans do, so every cell was searched and replayed on
the new maps. Every cell's paper is on its curve (`Tools/PlayTest/r65_paper.txt`; `BalanceLedgerTests` green).

**Shard Ridge's last boss** (round 64's open point 2). New script lever `bosscrowd` (`wave_tuning.txt`: the share of a boss
wave's budget its crowd keeps on that cell; the rule's 0.6 otherwise), set to 0.35 on Shard Ridge Hard and Psycho. The crowd
gives way and the boss grows to what the round-64 rule asks of it (two fifths of what the expected player can deal in its
walk): Hard **932 -> 2197**, Psycho 1337 -> 2550 (and its Core Wisp 1364 -> 1766), so Psycho's last boss is above Hard's
again on this level. No other boss of the campaign moved (`Tools/PlayTest/r65_bosses.txt`; Landing Site Psycho's three by
1 to 4 % with its waves).

**Where it falls** (the probe: `ProbeTrace` now writes a line per boss into every run's trace, `Tools/PlayTest/r65_boss_fates.py`
collects them; the five searched plans on three seeds): Shard Ridge Hard's Brood Mother falls at **0.55 to 0.57 of the
road, 111 to 118 s after it came in, in 15 runs of 15**, past the first gate (0.14 of the road), and the cell is won 3/3 by
every plan. Honest reading: it fell that deep before as well. On round 64's waves with this round's maps the 932-point boss
fell at 0.40 to 0.41 after 82 to 86 s, and on Easy the 699-point one falls at 0.56. The searched plans defend Shard Ridge's
*second* gate (0.72, behind the join of its two roads; their towers stand at 0.39 to 0.95 of the road) and leave the first
gate to itself, and a gun shoots whatever is furthest along, so a boss that comes in behind its crowd walks until it is the
last thing on the road. Where a boss falls says where the defence stands more than how tough the boss is: on Landing Site,
Glass Meadows and Quartz Flats the plans stand at the first gate and the bosses die in front of it (Glass Meadows Hard's
Brood Mother, 1531: 0.05 of the road, 6 to 9 s in, 0 runs of 9 at the gate; the table of all 42 bosses is in
Docs/BALANCE.md). Against Remco's own defence at the first gate (a Cannon at level 2 and a Gun Turret at level 3, about 96
damage a second and some 8 s of fire before the gate) the 349 he met was gone in under four seconds and round 64's 932 fell
about at the gate; **2197 reaches the gate and hammers it for a quarter of a minute**. A defence that lands more than about
260 a second on it there still stops it short, and a boss tough enough for that does not fit under its wave's cap.

**The rule for every cell that was taken back.** First I thinned the crowd of every boss wave of the campaign
(`BossWaveShare` 0.6 -> 0.35) and raised what a boss asks alone on Hard and Psycho (0.4 / 0.45 -> 0.5), reasoning that a
boss asks single-target fire and a row of Cannons has least of that. The paper liked it; the full pipeline did not:
mid-level bosses carried their wave's multiplier up (Glass Meadows Hard's Core Wisp 877 -> 1425, Crysium Vein Psycho's
2534 -> 4149), acceptance fell from 11 to 9 of 24, Landing Site Hard's searched plans fell from 2/3 to 1/3 at the bigger
last boss, and the Cannon row won Landing Site Hard and Psycho 3/3 all the same. So the rule is back at 0.6 and 0.4 / 0.45
and the thinner crowd is a lever per cell. That pass cost about fifty minutes of machine time; its tables are in
`Logs/r65/` (`cells_globalrule.txt`, `acceptance_globalrule.txt`, `boss_fates_replay_globalrule.txt`).

**The Cannon row (round 64's open point 1): not fixed, and not fixable with Landing Site's own creatures.** It still wins
Landing Site Hard and Psycho 3/3 with three stars and a full base. Why, in numbers:
- Per 100 coins at level 1 a Cannon lands 25 every 1.6 s on up to three creatures: 47 damage a second on a pile. Two Gun
  Turrets for the same money land 29, and a fifth of that on armour. Creatures stop at a gate, so there is always a pile.
- Landing Site sends two ground species: Skitters (a pile at the gate) and Cragbacks (armour). The Cannon is the best gun
  per coin against both. The levers the builder has (plated, swarm, tempo, raid, scale) only move the mix of those two:
  more Cragbacks is what made the Cannon the answer, and fewer hands the level back to the Gun Turret row, which lost this
  cell only once armour counted (round 64).
- In round 64's Hard record the seven Cannons of the row (four at level 2) dealt all 5681 hit points of wave 11 with the
  gate barely touched; on a pile they land some 570 damage a second together. The bigger last boss of the first pass
  (1843) died at 0.11 of the road, in the first gate's queue, 22 to 24 s in, for the Cannon row as for the creative bot.
- What a Cannon cannot do: aim up, and hit something that does not stop (its shell flies at 5 a second and does not home).
  Neither is in Landing Site's bestiary. So the composition that breaks the row is one Remco has to choose (open point 1).

### Open points (round 65)

1. **The Cannon row still wins Landing Site Hard and Psycho** (and Glass Meadows Medium). No mix of Skitters and Cragbacks
   breaks it (see 5). The choices: (a) **flyers on Landing Site's Hard and Psycho** (Remco's own note of 2026-10-29,
   "difficulty can add air waves"): a Cannon cannot aim up, so the row needs Gun Turrets; but the Flak is Glass Meadows'
   reward, so those raids must be small enough for Gun Turrets at their 0.2 against the sky, and Voss's Skyray scan names a
   Flak the player may not own yet; (b) **the Cannon's data**, with the numbers above as the reason (three creatures a shell
   at 100 coins beats two Gun Turrets on every pile: two a shell, or 120 coins); (c) **a creature for the early levels that
   does not stop at a gate or outruns a shell** (the Roller comes in level 6). I did not choose for Remco.
2. **A gun on the plain behind a plateau still fires through it** (per level 12 to 71 of the build cells within reach of raised ground: Landing Site 18 of 120, Glass Meadows 38 of 194, Shard Ridge 71 of 172, Fault Line 12 of 100, Quartz Flats 19 of 138, Crysium Vein 29 of 169; `Tools/PlayTest/r65_line_of_fire.txt`). They are four or
   more cells from the road and no plan spot; closing them would dot the ground behind every plateau with blocked cells.
   A line-of-sight rule in targeting would end it for good, at a cost per shot and a change the balance model must learn.
3. **Creatures out of a nest walk straight to the road at road height** (they always did): on today's six levels no nest's walk crosses raised ground or its slope (0 of 10; the line-of-fire report counts them), but a map that puts a plateau between a nest and the road would have them wade through it.
4. **The look of high ground** is a first pass (see the stills): 0.33 high, a glowing seam, a different top. Higher is not
   possible with muzzles this low (a taller plateau closes its own second row); a tower model with a higher muzzle, or a
   plinth for towers on high ground, would allow it.
5. **Bosses in the replays walk half the road** because the guns shoot whatever is furthest along and the boss comes in
   behind its crowd. Whether Shard Ridge's boss now feels like a fight against a defence that focuses it is Remco's to
   judge in play; on paper it asks 0.40 of the expected player alone.

## Round 66: ten upgrade tiers opened per continent, Spencer's repair drone and armour, the blade that burns red, Voss explains the upgrade screen (2026-11-15)

Not committed (the curator commits). No full generator run: `Tools/PlayTest/Scripts/ApplyRound66.cs` (the upgrades, the hero's
gear art, the story's hints) writes what the changed generator now would; the waves were not touched and no solve was
needed (section 1). No Blender (the armour plates are meshes built in code), no packages, the armour factor table and the
Game view's resolution untouched, `Docs/RELEASE_GAPS.md` and `Docs/STORY_REVIEW.md` untouched. Remco's save `progress.json`
(MD5 **463303aa28769c0934c10dc303967162** at the start) was copied aside before every Play Mode run and restored after;
identical after each run and at the end; the dev backup untouched. Editor play runs strictly one after another; EditMode on
the spare clone w6. The numbers: Docs/BALANCE.md "Round 66"; commands: Docs/COMMANDS.md "Round 66".

### 1. Ten tiers, opened per continent

- **Data.** Every permanent upgrade has ten tiers (`UpgradeDefinition._costs`); the base turrets (three steps) and the extra
  harvest drone (two) keep their own. Which tier is open on which continent is a list on the upgrade catalogue
  (`UpgradeCatalog._tiersPerContinent` = **4 / 6 / 8 / 9 / 10**), written by the generator from
  `BalanceRules.UpgradeTiersPerContinent`, which the progression model shops under as well. No continent is named in code:
  the player's cap is what the furthest continent they can enter opens (`CampaignRules.ReachedRegion` /
  `UpgradeTierCap`, read by `UpgradeTiers`), and `ProgressService.TryBuyUpgrade(upgrade, tierCap)` refuses a tier above it.
- **Prices.** First tier x 1 / 2 / 3 / 4.4 / 6 / 8 / 10.4 / 13.2 / 16.4 / 20 (`BalanceRules.UpgradeTierCostCurve`,
  `UpgradeEconomy.TierCosts`): a first tier of 5 costs 5, 10, 15, 22, 30, 40, 52, 66, 82, 100. Tiers 1-3 are the old three
  at the old price and the old worth (the bonus per tier is unchanged and stays linear).
- **The economy** (Docs/BALANCE.md "Round 66" has the tables). Crystal Plains opens 1352 research (tiers 1-4 of its six
  towers, the base, the gates and Spencer); its budget stays 748, which is 55% of that (`BalanceRules.ResearchBudgetShare`,
  the rule for the later continents' budgets). All twenty levels pay 150 on Easy, 300 on Medium, 450 on Hard, 750 on
  Psycho, 1650 on all four: one difficulty never buys all four tiers, all four together do with about 300 to spare. The
  six levels that exist pay 36 / 72 / 108 / 180 (396 together). Projected to tier 10: 21 328 research opened over five
  continents against 25 839 earned on every difficulty; the player of every difficulty holds the cap on every continent.
- **The Crystal Plains balance did not move.** The model's player per cell is identical before and after
  (`R66PlayerStates.cs`, 24 cells: research, every upgrade level, the mean tower bonus), so `ExpectedUpgradeBonus` and
  every stored wave are as they were; nothing was solved, measured or replayed. The calibration's input and shape
  hashes did move (upgrade tiers, the model's sources), so the yardstick-only fit ran again on w6 (identical in every
  number) and `balance_pipeline.sh apply-keep` stamped the calibration current with every factor kept. Why, and where the model is now knowingly a little kind (Spencer's
  gear is not in the model's shopping): BALANCE.
- **The save.** No format change and no migration step: the three old tiers are the first three of the ten, so a save's
  levels carry over as they are. `Round66Tests.OldSave_LoadsIntoTheTenTierModel_WithoutLoss` asserts it on a save shaped
  like Remco's, and `SaveCopy_LoadsIntoTheTenTierModel_WithoutLoss` ran on a copy of his real file
  (`Tools/PlayTest/r66_save_copy.json`, deleted afterwards): Base turrets 1, Gate strength 2, Gun Turret damage 2,
  9 research and 7 power all kept, nothing above the cap.
- **The upgrade screen.** A row is the upgrade's name over a strip of ten pips: bought (lit), open (dark), or a small
  amber padlock for a tier that waits for a later continent. Top right of the panel: "Tier 5 opens on Ashen Reach" (the
  continent's name from the campaign's regions). A row whose open tiers are all bought shows its value and
  "tier 5 opens on Ashen Reach" in amber and cannot be pressed; the focus skips it as it skips an unaffordable row. Four
  rows fit (Spencer has four). The tile's bar runs over all ten tiers (it never shrinks); its gold star now means
  "everything open so far is bought", so MASTERED is celebrated per continent. The purchase celebration is unchanged.

### 2. Spencer's gear

Two new research upgrades in his group, ten tiers each, gated like every other: **Repair drone** (`Hero_RepairDrone`,
`UpgradeTarget.HeroRegen`, +25% healing per tier: 6.0 to 7.5 hp/s at tier 1, 12 hp/s at tier 4) and **Armour**
(`Hero_Armour`, `UpgradeTarget.HeroArmour`, 5% off every hit per tier: 20% at tier 4, half at tier 10). His old "Armour"
row was his health and is now called **Health** (same id `Hero_Health`, same numbers). The effects travel in
`HeroGear` (Core) on `PlayerModifiers`; `Commander` takes the armour off every hit he takes (a strike, his share of the
gate's hit, slime) while the gate still gets what it got, and multiplies his own regeneration; the pause after a hit is
unchanged. How it looks is `HeroGearArtDefinition` (`Data/Art/Story/MercerGearArt.asset`), read only by the views:
- **The companion** (`HeroCompanionDrone`): the repair drone's own model at 45%, hovering at his left shoulder, bobbing,
  its rotors turning, trailing a little when he walks or flies. While his health climbs it lays the painted tool cone
  on his chest with a soft glow where it lands; both fade in and out over 0.35 s. It also stands beside him in the
  upgrade screen's turning preview as soon as it is bought.
- **The armour** (`HeroArmourPlates`, `ArmourPlateMesh`): framed plates in the suit's colours with a glowing ridge,
  built in code and fixed to his bones: upper arms at tier 1, the chest at 2, the forearms at 3, the thighs at 4, the
  shins at 5; from there they grow to 130% at tier 10. The generator seats each plate on the suit's surface in the idle
  pose (it measures the posed mesh along the plate's outward line), so nothing floats; caps on his own shoulder pieces
  were tried and dropped, they floated beside the helmet. The preview shows the plates the moment a tier is bought.

### 3. The blade at its top tier

When the blade damage upgrade stands at the highest tier open to the player (tier 4 on Crystal Plains), `HeroGear.BladeAtTop`
is set and `HeroArtView` lights the blade in `MasterBladeColor` (red) with a `BladeAura`: a long soft glow laid along the
blade and turned to the camera, a rounder glow about its middle, and a few embers. All of it is laid from the blade's
own base and tip after the body is posed and scales with the blade's ignition, so it follows every cut and comes and
goes with the blade. Not an upgrade of its own; when the next continent opens more tiers the blade is cyan again until
it is topped again (deliberate, see the open points).

### 4. Spencer in his card

The tile picture used the tower framing, which is half his height: he stood half outside it. `IconFraming.FittedCard`
centres and zooms the picture on the model itself (`ModelIconRenderer.FitTo`); the towers and drones keep their framing.

### 5. Dr. Voss explains the upgrade screen (the coordinator's extra task)

The first time the screen opens in a save, Voss says how it works in four lines (`Dlg_Tip_UpgradeScreen` on the story,
written by the generator; the tier number in his third line is the rules' cap): research points and difficulty, tiers

### 1. The audit: what was decided per weapon instead of by a rule

Every damage source (13 towers with hybrids, gate gun and base turret; Spencer's blaster, sword and shockwave; the attack
drone; mine, barrel, lava ball, ground drone) and every creature (41, bosses included) was read from the data and played
through `RoleMatrix` (`Tools/PlayTest/r67_role_matrix.txt`).

  Railgun, Cryo, Storm Rifle and Cryo Beam all landed in full on flyers. The hero's weapons, the drone and the path
  objects had no layer share at all.

  the flyers it caught at the ground share.

## Round 69: crash-safe saves, settings in their own file, string tables (English only) (2026-11-16)

Not committed. No full generator run (one targeted step: `Tools/Generate/Localisation Tables`), no Blender, no packages
(no Unity Localization package: an own string-table system), the Game view untouched, save folder and product name
unchanged. Remco's save (MD5 42fbe06b38e133cecfe2014def5c833c) copied aside before the one Play Mode run; after it the
`settings.json` (+ `.bak`) the run wrote were removed again, so the folder is as it was and his first launch does the
migration itself. Two helper agents moved the UI literals of the menu screens and of the in-level UI; the rest was done here.

### What changed

1. **Crash-safe saves** (`Platform/FileSaveService.cs`): writes go to `<key>.json.tmp`, then `File.Replace` swaps it in
   and keeps the previous good file as `<key>.json.bak`. Loading catches empty, whitespace, truncated and malformed files
   (JsonUtility's `ArgumentException`) and IO errors: the damaged file is copied to `<key>.json.damaged`, the backup is
   loaded with a warning, and with no usable backup the key loads as missing (fresh save, warning). Boot can no longer
   throw on a bad save.
2. **Settings split** (`Economy/SettingsData.cs`, `SettingsService.cs`): volumes, camera speed, edge scrolling, radar,
   HUD margin, plus the new language and mute-in-background, live in `settings.json`. First boot after the split reads the
   old progress file as `SettingsData` (same field names) and writes `settings.json` at once; the fields are gone from
   `ProgressData` (the next progress save drops them; `ProgressData.Version` unchanged, nothing else in it moves). Setters
   only change memory and raise `Changed`; `Flush()` writes when the options panel closes (Back, B/Esc, replay intro,
   language change, destroy), when the pause menu leaves its Sound/Camera page or closes, and on quit.
3. **Localisation plumbing** (`Core/Localization/`: `Loc`, `ILocalizationService`, `StringTableService`,
   `StringTableParser`, `LanguageInfo`; tables in `Resources/Localization/<lang>.<part>.txt`): 426 UI keys (menus 182, level
   156, options/pause/controls 87, core 1) and 554 data keys, 980 strings in all, English text unchanged. Definitions keep
   keys in their text fields and resolve them in their getters; `DialogueSegment`, `BossBark`, `MapNode` and `MapRegion`
   got a private field (`FormerlySerializedAs`) behind a resolving property; struct fields read in one place
   (`CutsceneShot.TitleCard`, `TowerLevel.StepName`, `BossPhase.Name`, level reward credit/story, repeat barks) are
   resolved there. The generator keeps its English spec; its new last data step "Localisation"
   (`Editor/LocalisationTables.cs`) turns every text field into a key and writes `en.data.txt`; property paths for
   segments, barks and map names updated in the generator. `Editor/LocalisationImportWatcher.cs` drops the editor's cached
   tables when a table imports. How to add a language: `Docs/LOCALISATION.md`.
4. **Options**: new rows "Mute in background   On/Off" (default on, `Boot/AppFocusAudio.cs` silences the listener while
   the window has no focus) and "Language   English" (steps through every table; a change reloads the main menu). The
   controls page is built from keys when it opens.
5. **Controller notice** (`UI/ControllerNotice.cs`, persistent "Session" object made by the bootstrapper): "Controller
   disconnected. Reconnect it to continue." on `DeviceLost`, "Controller connected." for 2.5 s on `DeviceRegained`.
