### What changed

1. **Display and graphics page** (Options > "Display and graphics", `UI/DisplayOptionsPage.cs`): display mode (full screen /
   borderless / windowed) and resolution (`Screen.resolutions`, one entry per size) as stepped sliders plus "Apply display
   settings", which puts the mode on screen and opens "Keep these display settings?" (`UI/DisplayConfirmPrompt.cs`: Keep,
   Revert, B/Esc reverts, 10 s in unscaled time reverts by itself); v-sync on/off; frame-rate cap 30/60/120/unlimited (the
   label says when v-sync overrides it); graphics quality High/Low; screen shake 0-100%. The window, resolution, v-sync, cap
   and quality rows show only where `IPlatformSettings.HasDisplayOptions` (PC); shake shows everywhere. Window and v-sync
   changes are skipped inside the editor (`DisplayOptions`), so the Game view and the project's quality settings are never
   touched; they apply in a player build, at boot (`Bootstrapper.ApplyDisplay`, the window only when the player chose
   something other than borderless at desktop size) and live.
2. **Quality profile for players:** `PcPlatformSettings(lowQuality)` takes every quality switch of the low profile and keeps
   the PC's quit, margin and window behaviour; `QualityProfileSwitch` (registered by the bootstrapper on PC) re-registers the
   platform settings and `ModelQuality` and sets the LOD bias and the tilt-shift pass at once; the next level is built with
   it. The Boot checkbox `_lowQuality` still simulates the console (`SwitchPlatformSettings`, no choice).
3. **Screen shake:** every `CameraShaker` kick and the cutscene shake cues are scaled by `SettingsService.ScreenShakeScale`.
4. **Settings file** (`SettingsData` version 2): `DisplayMode`, `ResolutionWidth/Height` (0 = desktop), `VSync` (on),
   `FrameRateCap` (0 = none), `LowQuality`, `ScreenShakePercent` (100), `BindingOverrides` (Input System override JSON).
   Older files get the defaults (seen on the seed from Remco's progress file in the play runs: v-sync on, shake 100).
5. **Pad families and hot-swap:** `PadLayout.PlayStation`; `PadLayoutResolver` reads the Input System layout chain of the
   pad in use (DualShock/DualSense -> PlayStation, Switch Pro -> Nintendo, XInput -> Xbox, unknown -> the platform default);
   `InputSystemProvider` follows it when a different pad presses a button or moves a stick, swaps the names table
   (`Glyphs_PlayStation.asset` is new: Cross, Circle, Square, Triangle, L1/R1, L2/R2, Options, Create; the keyboard table
   gained short names for modifiers, arrows and navigation keys) and raises `ActiveDeviceChanged`, so every prompt redraws.
   Verified in Play Mode with virtual pads and real queued button events: keyboard -> DualSense (Cross) -> XInput (A) ->
   DualSense again.
6. **Button glyphs drawn in code** (`UI/Glyphs/`): `GlyphPainter` draws discs, pills, triggers, key caps, sticks, the d-pad
   and a mouse with signed-distance edges; letters come from `StrokeFont` (A-Z, 0-9, key symbols, arrows); `GlyphCatalog`
   maps a control to the Xbox letters in their colours, the PlayStation shapes, the Nintendo letters, or a key cap carrying
   the key's name; `PromptGlyphs` caches one sprite per glyph. Used by: the hero quick bar (a badge on each icon), the
   dialogue buttons (Voss and every speaker), the cutscene skip chip, the planet map help line (`PromptLine`: glyphs inside
   the localised sentence, shrinks to fit), and the controls page. A missing glyph falls back to the printed name.
7. **Controls page with rebinding** (`UI/ControlsPage.cs`, replaces the hardcoded Xbox table): every action with its pad and
   keyboard glyph from the live bindings and the pad family in use; pick a cell, press a button or key (Esc cancels, 8 s
   gives up); a control another action holds is swapped to that action, so nothing is ever unbound; "Reset to defaults";
   the menu stops listening while it waits, so the press does not also click. Overrides go to `settings.json` when the
   options close and load at boot; text that is unreadable or leaves confirm, cancel or pause without a control falls back
   to the defaults (`InputSystemProvider.Rebinding.cs`, `IInputBindings`). The fixed controls (cursor, camera, zoom) are
   listed under the table with their glyphs. Verified end to end with a virtual XInput pad: Confirm -> Y, Speed and Codex
   swapped to A, overrides written to the settings file on closing the options.
8. **Control schemes:** `GameInput.inputactions` has a Gamepad and a Keyboard&Mouse scheme and every plain binding a group.
9. **IL2CPP prepared, not built:** `BuildScript.BuildWindowsIl2Cpp` (menu `Tools/Build/Windows Player (IL2CPP)`, output
   `Builds/WindowsIl2Cpp`, backend IL2CPP and stripping Low for that build only, restored afterwards) and `Assets/link.xml`
   (`Game.Economy`, `Game.Platform`, `Unity.InputSystem` kept whole). This editor has only the Mono player variations

     the overview). `GameAction.SkipWave` -> `GameAction.CallWave` (value 6). The developer gate on the keys
     (`InputSystemProvider.DeveloperActions`) is gone. The controls page lists "Call next wave" for everyone, after Speed,
     rebindable on both devices. `DefaultBindingTests` allows two actions on one control only as a tap/hold pair.

     line for 1.8 s (`hud.early_bonus`). The money is added as it is (not scaled by the difficulty's income share).
   - Guard rails (`Levels/WaveCaller.cs`, why in `WaveCallBlock`): not before the first wave (the opening countdown is build
     time, data switch `AllowBeforeFirstWave`), not while paused or while a story box, the codex, the briefing or the recon holds

     a bare test level uses the field defaults). Generator step "Wave call" (`ProjectGenerator.WaveCall.cs`).
   - The wave timeline is now a plain class (`Levels/WaveClock.cs`): countdowns, the running wave, and the win rule (every wave
     started and spawned, nothing alive). `LevelController` drives it; the waiting player's timeline is unchanged.

     (`ComingBoss`, "BOSS" on the wave line), and `BossWaveStarted` is raised only by a wave that brings a boss.

     `FastForwardAllowed` from developer mode): the rest of the running wave comes out at once and the next wave starts, no
     bonus, no rules. No key or HUD icon. The PlayMode tests that used `SkipWaveRequested` use it under the new name.

  more tempting, or scale it by the difficulty's income share.

## Balance stage 1: the headroom metric tested (2026-11-16)

Not committed. Test and tool code only: no gameplay or data change, the old pipeline untouched, no generator, no Blender, no
packages, the Game view untouched. No Play Mode in the editor; every run was on the silent clones w1-w5 (EditMode on w6).
Remco's save MD5 42fbe06b38e133cecfe2014def5c833c before and after every batch; no `settings.json`; no worker left running.
Full write-up: Docs/BALANCE_HEADROOM.md. Commands: Docs/COMMANDS.md, "Balance stage 1: headroom".

### What was built

- `HeadroomProbeTests.Measure_Headroom` (PlayMode, explicit): the finale probe's bisection on an ordinary level. Per level,
  difficulty, reference player and seed it finds the largest uniform health multiple the player still wins at (3 %
  precision), through a runtime copy of the level; it records every run with a per-wave leak line and the base health.
- Reference players that read no model: careless (`naive`), sensible (new `PlayStyle.Sensible`: the affordable buyer who
  buys the counter tower by the role table when the preview shows armour or flyers), skilled (the best replayed plan's
  build order as a fixed script), the mono rows, and the sensible player on a plain save.
- `Tools/PlayTest/headroom.sh "<nodes>" "<difficulties>"` runs it on the clones and writes `headroom_records.txt` and
  `headroom.txt` (`headroom_report.py`).

### Result: stage 1 did not pass its stop rules

Landing Site and Shard Ridge, four difficulties, seeds 1-3: 1450 runs, 87 minutes of wall clock.

- **Monotonicity fails:** 17 of 78 scanned units have more than one win/lose crossover (flip-back zone 5 to 41 % wide).
- **Reproducibility:** the same seed repeats exactly on another clone (8 of 8 edges). Across seeds H is within 5 % in only
  3 of 20 cell-rungs (sensible 3-13 % on Landing Site, 13-221 % on Shard Ridge; skilled 0-66 %; careless 79-622 %).
- **Sanity:** the Cannon row wins Landing Site Hard and Psycho (1.14, 1.50), off-role rows lose, every obvious row on Shard
  Ridge loses at any health down to a tenth, skilled is above sensible in 8 of 8 cells. But careless beats sensible on
  Landing Site, and H does not fall steadily from Easy to Psycho.
- **Rescale:** per seed within 1.7 % of target; the cell's seed spread stays.
- H medians (careless / sensible / skilled): Landing Site 1.62 / 1.16 / 1.75, 1.54 / 1.22 / 1.26, 1.00 / 0.84 / 1.14,
  0.52 / 0.53 / 1.16; Shard Ridge <0.10 / 0.41 / 1.26, <0.10 / 0.84 / 1.58, <0.10 / 0.54 / 1.58, <0.10 / 0.27 / 1.26.

### Verification

- Compile clean. EditMode on w6: **1122 / 1069 passed / 0 failed / 53 skipped** (unchanged).
- All worker batches passed with 0 probe errors.

### Open decision for Remco

Stage 2 (the 24-cell table replacing the gate) should not start as written. Proposed instead: a short stage that uses fixed
build orders as the ruler (the most stable rung) on five seeds for the same two levels, and goes on only if the spread drops
under about 10 %. Options and reasons are in Docs/BALANCE_HEADROOM.md, "What this means".

### Not done

- The other four levels. Why Shard Ridge Easy reads harder than Medium for the sensible player.
- A pooled estimate over seeds (only median and range are reported).
- No separate experiment on why edges flip back; the explanation in the write-up is read from the records.

## Balance stage 1b: a continuous pressure score tested (2026-11-17)

Not committed. Test and tool code only: no gameplay or data change, the stage 1 pipeline untouched (one `headroom.sh` unit
re-run after the change: passed, same side of the edge as on 2026-11-16), no generator, no Blender, no packages, the Game
view untouched. No Play Mode in the editor; every run was on the silent clones w1-w5 (EditMode on w6). Remco's save MD5
42fbe06b38e133cecfe2014def5c833c before and after every batch; no `settings.json`; no worker left running.
Full write-up: Docs/BALANCE_HEADROOM.md, "Stage 1b". Commands: Docs/COMMANDS.md, "Balance stage 1b: pressure".

### What was built

- `PressureProbeTests.Measure_Pressure` (PlayMode, explicit): a reference player plays a level at fixed health multiples, no
  bisection. New rung `typical`: the sensible bot's seed 1 build order replayed as a fixed script.
- `BotRun.Advance()`: per wave the health spawned, that health weighted by how far each creature got, and the health that
  reached the base. Every run is recorded with it, base and gate damage, and the build order taken.
- `Tools/PlayTest/pressure.sh "<nodes>" "<difficulties>"` runs it on the clones and writes `pressure_records.txt` and
  `pressure.txt` (`pressure_report.py`; the stop rules are constants there, fixed before the batch).
- Pressure P = A + D (0 to 2): A = mean over the waves of the health-weighted share of the road covered, D = base health lost.

### Result: the stop rules are not met; the score is two-valued

Landing Site and Shard Ridge, four difficulties, seeds 1-5, multiples 0.5 to 2: 1120 runs, 58 minutes on five clones.

- **(a) Monotone, at least 95 % of curves: fails by one curve.** 151 of 160 (94.4 %). Scripts 78 of 80, sensible bot 34 of 40.
- **(b) Seed spread of P at the data under 10 % for the skilled script: fails.** 1 of 8 cells (Shard Ridge Easy 0.9 %); the
  others 17 to 151 %.
- **(c) Known facts: holds.** Cannon row 5 of 5 on every Landing Site difficulty; sensible player 0 of 5 on Shard Ridge Hard
  and Psycho; the air raid hits the base in wave 12 or 13 on nearly every seed.
- Why: a won run ends with a full base and a lost one at zero, so P is win/lose plus a small term (Landing Site Hard,
  skilled: 0.09, 0.10, 0.10, 0.11, then 1.22). Only Shard Ridge Hard and Psycho degrade gradually.
- Seeds won at the data (skilled / typical / sensible): Landing Site 5/5/5, 2/5/5, 5/0/1, 3/0/0; Shard Ridge 5/0/1, 5/2/3,
  5/0/0, 5/0/0.

### Findings (causes, not fixed)

- **Landing Site wave 7:** the seed draws which of the two nests its nest group leaves. On seeds 3, 4 and 5 a creature comes
  up behind the first gate; a player with no gun at the far gate loses that gate and the base at any health (skilled script
  on Medium: lost on those seeds even at x0.5). This is stage 1's "seed 3 loses at every multiple".
- **Shard Ridge Easy harder than Medium (sensible):** not health (Easy spawns 68 % of Medium's). On Medium the flyers show in
  the preview during wave 10 and the Rocket is bought then, on all five seeds. On Easy the first flyers come in wave 12
  without an introduction wave, the bot has just spent its wave 10 money, buys nothing in waves 11 and 12 and no Rocket on
  4 of 5 seeds; from wave 13 the preview is clear, it stops saving, and the Skyrays on the base finish it (also at x0.5).
- **Careless beats sensible on Landing Site:** the careless rule alternates the ground guns, so half its guns are Cannons, the
  strongest row there; the sensible rule's "dearest affordable step" ends at one Cannon and eight Gun Turrets. On Hard the
  sensible bot stops building after wave 5 (3 guns, 601 coins earned against 1740, 213 on repairs).

### Verification

- Compile clean (only the old CS0618 in `Tests/PlayMode/BalanceProbeTests.cs`).
- EditMode on w6: **1122 / 1069 passed / 0 failed / 53 skipped** (unchanged).
- The pressure batch and both smoke batches passed with 0 probe errors.

### Open decisions for Remco

- Do not gate on P or H with percentage bands. Proposed instead: read the probe as seeds won out of five at x0.8, x1 and x1.25
  (roomy / tight / too hard, plus "lost at x0.5 = structural"), and first decide the three structural findings above.
- Landing Site: should a wave 7 creature be able to come up behind the first gate on some seeds?
- Shard Ridge Easy: an introduction wave before the first raid, as Medium has?
- The sensible bot needs two repairs before it stands for a real player again (keep saving while flyers are alive; do not let
  repairs starve the counter purchase). Test code, but it changes every "sensible" number.

### Not done

- The other four levels. A rerun-on-another-clone check for the pressure records (stage 1 showed the probe repeats per seed).
- Which of the two Landing Site nests lies behind the gate was not checked on the map.
- The purse per wave is not recorded, so "the Rocket was not affordable in time" on Easy is inferred from the build order.

### Item 2: Landing Site's wave 7 rift is authored

- New field `SpawnGroup.Nest` (0 = drawn, n = nest n of `LevelDefinition.Nests`, counted from 1), written by the generator's
  Waves step from `TroopSpec.Nest` (`Join(..., nest: n)`), honoured by `NestAssignment.Draw` (no draw for an authored
  group). Landing Site's rift Cragbacks name nest 1, (17,1), the rift behind the first gate. The second nest (10,8) stays in
  the layout and is simply never used, so it stays closed and unmarked; no map change.

  No multiplier, count or timing moved (the solve is otherwise idempotent; the other five wave assets are untouched).
- Validator rule (`LevelValidator.SmallNestGroup` = 2): a group of at most two walkers out of a nest, on a level with more
  than one nest of its element, must have an authored nest; an authored nest must be a nest of that element. Only Landing
  Site has such groups today (the small nest groups of C1_04 and C1_06 are flyers). Tests: two in

### Item 4: Shard Ridge Hard and Psycho: no data change

- The "swap" on Hard (wave 11 at 1.106, wave 12 at 0.212) is not a typing mistake and not in `wave_tuning.txt`. It comes out
  of the solve: a wave has one health multiplier for its crowd and its flyers, and `CampaignModel.CalibrateToHuman` trims a
  wave on its own when the paper player with the hero cannot hold it (the hero cap). On Hard that is wave 12 (ground
  pressure 1.09 in `balance_ledger.txt`, the highest before the late raids), on Medium wave 11. So Medium's soft first raid
  is the same accident, on the other wave. There is no "soft introduction raid" rule in the generator. Left as it is:
  swapping would put wave 12 over the hero cap in the model, and the measured cell does not need it.
- With the repaired bot Hard is no wall: sensible 5, 5 and 4 of 5 (two Rockets by wave 14, base hit in waves 12, 13 and 16
  without losing), skilled 5 of 5 everywhere. The condition for thinning the late raids (0 of 5 at x0.8) is not met.
  One criterion fails the other way: the sensible bot should lose most seeds at x1.25 and wins 4 of 5, so Hard is roomier
  than the critic's target.
- Psycho: skilled 5, 5, 4; sensible 1, 0, 0 (it loses in wave 16 on four seeds, with base hits from wave 12 on). That is
  inside the criterion (skilled 5 of 5 at x1, sensible may lose).

### Open findings and questions for Remco

1. **Landing Site Hard and Psycho became harder with the rift on every run.** Sensible on Hard at x1: 3 of 5 before, 0 of 5
   now (4 of 5 at x0.8). Skilled on Psycho at x1: 3 of 5 before, 1 of 5 now (5 of 5 at x0.8): the two rift Cragbacks of
   Psycho (wave multiplier 2.576) walk through both far gates and the base between waves 7 and 12 against the one Cannon
   the script adds there. Before, two seeds in five (one in four on Psycho) never met the rift. This is the honest price of
   the fix, and the same question as the next one.
2. **Is one unshot Cragback ending the level the intended price of ignoring the warning, also on Easy?** If not, the gentle
   version is a lever on the rift group alone (its health or, on Psycho, its count); nothing was decided or built.
3. **The sensible bot on Landing Site Hard sits on a knife edge**, and that is partly the bot: with armour in the preview it
   holds its purse for the first Cannon (100) from wave 6 on, its three light guns lose the gate in wave 6, and whether the
   purse reads 96 or 87 at the start of wave 7 decides the run (seed 3: 87, then a gate rebuilt every wave, no Cannon,
   650 coins earned against 1800 in a won run). The critic's repair rule is implemented as written; a player who buys a
   fourth light gun in wave 6 instead of saving is a different bot. Not tuned further.
4. **Shard Ridge Hard is roomy for the sensible bot (4 of 5 at x1.25).** Harden it, or accept?
5. **A soft first raid as a rule?** Today it is an accident of the hero cap. A script rule ("the first raid of a difficulty
   is never the tougher of the first two") would make it deliberate on every level; it fights the cap, so it needs a
   decision.
6. **The plan search is blind to a rift behind the gate.** Until it is not, the skilled rung leans on the reaction rule.
7. The solve stage rewrites the difficulty display names over the string keys of round 69 (found again, restored from git
   both times; Docs/COMMANDS.md has the pitfall). Worth a one-line fix in `GenerateDifficulties` in another round.

   turn" order or flyers hovering at the edge of the Flak's reach. So the scale change there is supported by the skilled

   Either the boss dies at the first gate or it walks through all four (gates lost in wave 17 on Medium: 360 and 446 in the

   off; the lever would be the boss's size on Medium (`_bossHealthScale` 1.18, set by the sizing rules of rounds 64 and
   65), and that is Remco's rule, so nothing was changed. Is an all-or-nothing boss wave the intended finale on Medium?

the two scales; the bot's knowledge and opening; affordability; the adaptive skilled rung and the health grid; the old
gates). Measurement was the goal: **no data changed except the two scales the critic named**, no tower, no map, no package,
no flyers on Landing Site, the Game view untouched. No Play Mode in the editor: every run was on the silent clones w1-w5
(EditMode on w6). The open editor was used for recompiles, one solve and one report script, each time after `editor_status`
read `playMode: stopped`. Remco's save MD5 42fbe06b38e133cecfe2014def5c833c before and after every batch; no
`settings.json`; no worker left running. Commands: Docs/COMMANDS.md, "Round 76".

### Item 1: the bot is frozen, records are stamped, batches are kept apart

- **The stamp.** Every pressure record now ends with `bot=<version>:<hash>;data=<hash>;game=<hash>`
  (`Assets/Tests/PlayMode/ProbeStamp.cs`): the reference players' version and a hash of everything that decides how they
  play (the probe's six source files, `plan_records.txt`, `Plans/*.json`), a hash of `Assets/_Project/Data`, a hash of
  `Assets/_Project/Scripts`. `ProbeStamp.BotVersion` is 2; the hash catches a rule change that forgot to bump it.
- **The tools refuse to mix.** `pressure_wins.py <after> <before>` refuses two files of different or unknown bots (every
  record of rounds 74 and 75 is unstamped, so those files can no longer be compared by accident) and says when the data
  differs as well; `pressure_report.py` refuses one file with more than one bot. `--mixed-bots` overrides, with a warning.
  The rule lives in `Tools/PlayTest/pressure_stamp.py`.
- **The noise rule is gone.** The round 75 table's "one or two seeds either way are noise" and its two echoes are corrected
  in place (a dated note under the table). Docs/COMMANDS.md never carried the rule; its round 76 section states the new
  one: a batch changes the bot or the data, never both.
- **A real source of run-to-run difference was found and removed while testing the stamp.** The critic concluded from the
  committed records that the probe is deterministic. It was, as long as a batch was dealt the same way. Played in another
  place of a worker's list, the same unit came out as a different game: Quartz Flats Hard, skilled, seed 1 at the data
  earned 2224, 2130 and 2105 coins in three plays, diverging in wave 1 (30.89 against 31.03 health-weighted advance). Cause:
  `BalanceProbeTests.Probe` set the fixed 0.2 s step only after the level scene had loaded, so the level's first frames ran
  on the wall clock and the first wave started a fraction of a step earlier or later against the bot's one-second buying
  beat. The step is now set before the scene loads. Check (COMMANDS round 76): three units played twice, early and late in
  a clone's list, at two multiples (`pressure_r76_wobble_before_records.txt`, `..._after_...`). Before the fix the game
  clock differed in all six pairs and the game itself in three (advance, purse, coins; one pair lost five waves apart).
  After it every field of all six pairs is identical except the gate-damage sum, which differs in its fourth decimal in
  three pairs (a float sum over the run, not a different game).
  So the critic's point 3 stands and is now true by construction, not by batch layout: identical batches of rounds 74 and
  75 reproduced because their units sat in the same places. Records of before this round carry that wobble when
  re-dealt (another seed count, another multiple list); one more reason not to compare them with today's.

### Item 3: the sensible bot knows what the game tells a player, and opens for it (bot version 2, frozen)

Test code (`BalanceProbeTests.SensibleAct`, `OpenForRoster`, `SizeCounterDemand`, `SellForFirstCounter`, `GuardRearRift`;
`BotRun`). What changed against round 75's bot:

- **Knowledge.** It reads the level's Codex roster (`LevelRoster.Collect`: the creatures this level and difficulty send;
  `BotRun.RosterTraits`) from second zero, and the field: living creatures, the base, the gates, a rift's marker and its
  opening. It no longer reads any wave's contents: `PreviewCount` and `ComingCounterTraits` (the current and the next
  wave) are deleted. A trait counts once it has been met on the field (`BotRun.SeenTraits`), and stays known.
- **Opening.** With plated creatures in the roster and no gun made for armour standing, the next gun bought is the Cannon
  (it shoots every walker, so nothing waits). With flyers in the roster and no sky gun standing it keeps a Flak's price
  back (`BotRun.HeldBack`) once a ground gun stands, and spends only what is above it; repairs leave the held coins alone
  too. It stops holding when the last wave's bounties would pay for a Flak (a purse that refills within a wave needs no
  coins kept back): without that the pilot showed 120 coins idle for ten waves on Shard Ridge Hard, where the flyers come
  in wave 11 and round 74's bot won without any reserve.
- **Counters by sight.** The first Flak or Cannon is bought when the first flyer or plated creature is alive. The counters
  grow at most once a wave when the field shows half as many again as they were sized for (the wave's peak is remembered),
  and after a wave in which the trait cost the base or a gate health, as before.
- **The rift.** Without a preview it reacts when a rift behind the defence gate is seen breaking open (state `Opening` or
  `Open`: the marker is there from second zero, Voss warns at the opening), with the Cannon when the roster holds plated
  walkers. The skilled rung keeps the wave-ahead reaction (it knows the level).
- **The sale is the emergency only**: flyers on the base, the base lost health with them there (`BotRun.FlyersBitingBase`),
  nothing that can aim up reaches the base, the purse short of the Flak.
- **Frozen.** `ProbeStamp.BotVersion = 2`. Two pilots (seed 1, x1, all 24 cells; `pressure_r76_pilot1/2_records.txt`)
  were played before the freeze: the first without the "stops holding" clause and with the wall-clock wobble, the second
  as frozen. Nothing was changed after the second pilot.

### Fault Line Medium traced (the critic's condition for touching its scale again)

One lost and one won run of the sensible rung at the data with `PR_KEEPTRACE=1` (seeds 1 and 3, the same build order up to
wave 14). In both the raid of wave 12 (three Skyrays at x1.84) arrives against one level 1 Flak at (34,9); the bot answers
the first bite with a second Flak on the next air spot, (33,9). On seed 3 all three Skyrays are dead after 5 bites (base
688 to 658). On seed 1 two die and **the third settles over the base where neither Flak reaches it: 53 bites in wave 13,
40 in wave 14, and so on until the base is gone** (700, 382, 142, 0), with both Flaks standing and the Gun Turrets far away
at the gate. (That it sits out of both Flaks' reach is inferred: a lone Skyray survives two full waves beside two Flaks;
the trace has no positions.) Nine of the cell's ten lost sensible runs, at every multiple from x0.8 to x1.25, have that
signature (base lost about 270 to 350, 240, 150 in waves 13 to 15; the tenth loses 600 to the boss wave), and so has the
skilled rung's one loss (seed 1, x1.25: its single Flak is on the same cell, (34,9)).
So the cell is decided by where one Skyray comes to rest, not by health: the critic's R3 in its purest form. The frozen
bot never puts a sky gun beside the base (its emergency gun there is for walkers) and never sells once a Flak stands; a
human would.

## Round 77: structure damage factor, first flyers after the bounties, a lighter Medium boss factor, Rotbloom at 28200 (2026-11-17)

Not committed. Remco's four decisions of 2026-11-17 as factors and rules in data, one at a time, each measured alone with
the frozen bot (stamp `bot=2:90273749`; the probe and bot code are untouched). Every run on the silent clones w1-w5
(EditMode on w6); the open editor only for recompiles, the solve stage and report scripts, each after `editor_status` read
`playMode: stopped`. Save MD5 42fbe06b38e133cecfe2014def5c833c before and after every batch, no `settings.json`, no worker
left. Commands: Docs/COMMANDS.md, "Round 77".

### 1. The structure damage factor

- **A multiplier already existed**: `DifficultyProfile._structureDamageMultiplier`, 0.6 / 0.75 / 1 / 1.4 (Easy to Psycho),
  on every bite (base, gates, towers, hero, boss powers). Remco's guess "0.6 on Easy and Medium" was made without knowing
  that, so it was read as a factor on top.
- **The multiplier cannot be the lever.** The siege model reads it, and Medium is the solver's base curve: setting Medium
  to 0.45 re-solved all four difficulties of all six levels (Medium +2 to +7 % health, Hard and Psycho moved too). So the
  solver answered softer bites with tougher creatures. The factor is therefore a field of its own:
  `DifficultyProfile._structureDamageFactor` (Range 0.1 to 1, `OnValidate` warns outside it), in play
  `StructureDamageMultiplier` = multiplier x factor (every caller unchanged), and the balance model reads
  `CalibratedStructureDamage` (the multiplier alone, `BalanceLedger.Stats`). With that the solve moves no wave for the factor.
- **Values** (`BalanceSheet.EasyStructureFactor` 0.75, `MediumStructureFactor` 0.6): both difficulties bite at 0.45 of a
  creature's damage (Easy 0.6 x 0.75, Medium 0.75 x 0.6); Hard 1 and Psycho 1.4 unchanged. Easy was given 0.75 only so it
  never bites harder than Medium; it was won everywhere before and after.
- **Measured on Medium** (overlay of `Medium.asset`, 180 runs each; seeds won at x0.8 / 0.9 / 1 / 1.12 / 1.25):

| Cell | Rung | 0.75 (round 76) | factor 0.8 (bites 0.6) | **factor 0.6 (bites 0.45)** | 0.6 on base and gates only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Landing Site Medium | skilled | 3 3 2 2 0 | 3 3 3 1 1 | 3 3 3 2 0 | 3 3 3 3 1 |
| Glass Meadows Medium | sensible | 3 2 2 0 0 | 3 3 2 1 0 | 3 3 3 0 0 | 3 3 3 0 0 |
| Glass Meadows Medium | skilled | 3 3 3 3 1 | 3 3 3 3 3 | 3 3 3 3 3 | 3 3 3 3 3 |
| Fault Line Medium | sensible | 2 1 1 1 0 | 3 1 1 1 1 | **3 3 3 3 3** | 3 1 1 1 1 |
| Fault Line Medium | skilled | 3 3 3 3 2 | 3 3 3 3 2 | 3 3 3 3 3 | 3 3 3 3 2 |
| Quartz Flats Medium | sensible | 1 0 0 0 0 | 3 0 0 0 0 | 3 0 0 0 0 | 3 0 0 0 0 |
| Quartz Flats Medium | skilled | 3 3 3 2 0 | 3 3 3 2 1 | 3 3 3 3 0 | 3 3 3 3 1 |
| Medium, runs won of 180 | | 134 | 146 | **155** | 149 |
| lost in the last wave from a base at 90 %+ | | 28 of 46 lost | 22 of 34 | 25 of 25 | 22 of 31 |

  (Landing Site sensible, Shard Ridge and Crysium Vein: 15 of 15 or one seed more in every column.)
- 0.6 wins most and is the only value that ends Fault Line Medium's resting Skyray (sensible 1 of 3 to 3 of 3 at the data).
  That fix comes from the softer bites on **towers** (the Flak survives): on base and gates alone the cell stays 1 of 3.
  Quartz Flats Medium's finale is untouched by any factor: wave 17 takes the whole base in one wave at every value.
- **The grace windows are distorted by any softening, and leaving the towers out does not help** (the brief's fallback was
  built and measured: 9 breaks against 10). A row without the counter falls by losing its base, so softer bites keep it a
  wave or two longer. No row wins. Seven allowances were added or lengthened, each with its reason in
  `GraceWindows.Allowances` and in Docs/COMBAT_RULES.md section 6: Glass Meadows Medium 1 -> 2 and Shard Ridge Medium 1 -> 2
  (armour), Fault Line Easy 1 (armour, new) and 1 -> 2 (air), Crysium Vein Easy 1 (air, new), Fault Line Medium 2 (air, new),
  Quartz Flats Medium 3 (armour, new; the last two also carry the moved raids of item 2). **Remco's call**: accept the later
  falls, or take the factor off Easy (three of the seven go away) or back to 0.8 on Medium.

### 2. First flyers on Easy and Medium only after the bounties pay one sky gun

- `BalanceRules.FlyersAfterBounties = { true, true, false, false }`, applied by `CampaignModel.BuildWaves` at every solve
  (`HoldFlyersUntilPayable`): while the first flyer wave plus the grace waves comes before the bounties reach the cheapest
  owned sky gun's price, the raids move a wave later together and flying troops wait (`WaveScriptSpec.FlyingTroopFloor`, new,
  apart from the Easy raid rule's floor, which stays as it was). The purse rule is one definition for the solver and the
  check: `Game.Balance.CounterPurse` (new), used by `CounterAffordability`. Medium is solved again from scratch when its raids

- **Audit: there is no per-level boss health number.** `_bossHealthScale` in the wave assets (Quartz Flats Medium 1.18
  among them) is the solver's output of four per-difficulty rules of round 64/65: a floor (`LevelBossHealthFloor`
  0.5 / 0.75 / 0.9 / 0.9 of book health), a share of the expected player's firepower the boss must ask alone
  (`LevelBossAlone` 0.2 / 0.3 / 0.4 / 0.45), a growth cap and a most-alone cap. That is already "a factor per difficulty

## Round 78: next-wave preview in the HUD, bot version 3 measured against version 2 (2026-11-17)

Not committed. Two parts, in the brief's order: the preview Remco approved on 2026-11-17, then the reference players
rebuilt on it (bot version 3), frozen and measured on all 24 cells. **No level data changed** (data stamp 645e4d4c, as in
round 77). No package, no generator run, the Game view untouched. Play Mode in the open editor only for the stills (each
time after `editor_status` read `playMode: stopped`; Remco's save copied aside first, MD5 42fbe06b38e133cecfe2014def5c833c
before and after every run, every `settings.json` the runs wrote deleted); every probe run on the silent clones w1-w5,
EditMode on w6. Commands: Docs/COMMANDS.md, "Round 78".

### A. The next-wave preview

- **What the player sees.** In the top strip, right of the wave line and left of the speed, pause, call and Codex icons:
  the word "Next" and one chip per creature type of the wave that starts next. A chip is the creature's picture (rendered
  from its model once per level, like the tower cards), with to its right a mark over a number: a **light blue wing** (the
  icon of the tower cards' air badge, so the creature's mark and the mark on the gun that answers it are one picture) on
  flyers, a **steel shield** (painted in code, `TraitBadgeArt`) on plated creatures, and "x12" for how many come on this
  difficulty. A **boss** is a red chip with the boss marker and the word BOSS, not its picture and not its name.
  The list is ranked: boss, flyers, plated, then the rest by number.
- **When.** From the opening countdown (it shows wave 1) to the start of the last wave; during a wave and between waves it
  shows the wave that comes next, which is exactly the wave "Call next wave" (round 73) would bring, because both read
  the same thing: `LevelContext.NextWave`, set by the level controller. After the last wave has started the strip is gone.
- **What stays a surprise.** The preview adds a creature type's groups up whatever their entrance, so it never says where
  anything comes from: a rift behind the gate is still announced by its marker on the ground and Voss's warning when it
  opens, as before (nothing of that was touched). What a boss calls in during the fight is not listed either, and a boss
  is not shown before it is met.
- **Fit.** The strip lives inside the top bar (60 units high in the bar's 72), so it covers no field and the keep-out of
  the world labels is unchanged. It measures its room between the wave line (which grows with "BOSS" and two-digit
  waves) and the icon row: chips are 106 wide when there is room (picture, then mark and number beside it), narrow down
  to 62 (mark and number slide over the picture's right side), then the word "Next" goes, and only then the last types
  (the plain walkers, by the ranking) fold into a "+N" chip. The first continent's widest waves list six types; six fit at
  the default margin and at a 5 % safe margin (without the label), and `WavePreviewTests` fails when a wave ever needs more.
  Numbers are at the HUD's readable size with a dark edge; nothing needs a pointer, a hover or a focus.
- **Data-driven.** `Game.Levels.WavePreview` (pure): the wave's groups through `WaveScheduler.CountOf`, so the numbers are the
  spawned numbers on the difficulty (a boss is one). Strings `hud.preview_next`, `hud.preview_count`, `hud.preview_more`,
  `hud.preview_boss` in `en.ui_level.txt` (no BOM).
- **Seen** (stills in `ArtSource/Previews/QA/`, each at 1920x1080 and 1280x720; the Game view itself as `_gameview`):
  - `r78_opening`: Landing Site before wave 1: "Wave 0/12", "Next", one chip (an orange Skitter, x12), "First wave in 2s"
    under the wave line. The chip's frame is faint against the bar; the creature and the number carry it.
  - `r78_plated`: wave 7 next: a Cragback (grey-brown dome) with the shield mark and x2, a Skitter x16.
  - `r78_boss`: wave 12 next: a red chip with the boss marker and BOSS, Cragback x9 with the shield, Skitter x36.
  - `r78_flyers`, `r78_flyers_gameview`: Crysium Vein, wave 7 next: a Shalebat with the wing mark and x5, Skitter x9,
    Roller x1. Three wide chips: picture left, mark top right, number bottom right.
  - `r78_five`, `r78_six`, `r78_six_gameview`: waves 13 and 18 next (five and six types, the widest of the continent): the
    chips narrow to about 90 units (five) and 70 units (six), the number slides over the picture's lower right corner and
    stays readable through its dark edge; with six the boss chip drops its marker and keeps the word. The strip ends 18
    units before the icons.
  - `r78_low_five`, `r78_low_six`: the Low (Switch) profile with a 5 % safe margin: five chips with the label, six
    without it (chips near their narrowest, 62 units); at 1280x720 the numbers are an 18 px font and read cleanly, the marks are
    about 16 px and are told apart by shape (wing, shield) more than by colour.
  - What is weak: the creature pictures are small (36 px at 720p) and stippled like their skins, so a species is told by
    colour and outline, not by detail (Skitter orange and spidery, Cragback a dome, Skyray blue and flat, Roller yellow and
    ribbed, Prowler brown); two brownish walkers side by side (Cragback, Prowler) are the closest pair, and the shield on
    the Cragback is what separates them. No names are shown (no hover on a pad); the Codex has them.
  - The High-profile stills look soft because the still helper draws the HUD through the tilt-shift pass; the Game view
    captures and the Low stills show the real sharpness (COMMANDS, "Round 78").
  - Console during every stills run: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- **EditMode:** `WavePreviewTests`, 14 cases: a type's groups add up whatever their entrance (road, second road, rift); the
  numbers are the scheduler's on the difficulty and a boss is one; the ranking; the wave's own order between equals; a
  boss's minions are left out; no wave lists nothing and clears an old list; a group without an enemy is skipped; the
  flyer and plated sums; the folding into "+N" for five strip widths; and every wave of every level and difficulty in the
  data lists something, at most six types, marked types first.

### B. Bot version 3

Test code only (`Assets/Tests/PlayMode`), then frozen: `ProbeStamp.BotVersion` is 3 and the hash now also covers
`SkilledPicks.cs` and `Tools/PlayTest/skilled_picks.txt`.

1. **The sensible rung reads the preview, and nothing more of a coming wave.** `BotRun.Preview` calls the same
   `WavePreview.Collect` on the same `LevelContext.NextWave` the HUD draws. A wing or plate mark in the next wave counts as
   that trait met (`NoteSeen`), so its counter is wanted one wave ahead, and the marked number sizes the counters
   (`SizeCounterDemand` takes the larger of the living and the previewed number). Everything else is version 2: the Codex
   roster, the opening for the roster, the Flak's price held back until the bounties refill it, the rift behind the gate
   answered when it opens (the preview does not say where creatures come from, so it cannot tell what a rift will send).
2. **A sky gun for a flyer the sky guns do not reach** (both rungs, `BalanceProbeTests.CoverBaseSky`). While flyers are
   biting the base (the base lost health with flyers on it) and one of them hangs where no standing gun made for the sky
   has it in range, one sky gun goes on the free build cell nearest that flyer: bought when the purse allows; else a sky
   gun is moved (sold and rebuilt there, when its sale closes the gap); else the cheapest other gun whose sale closes the
   gap is sold for it, never the last gun; else the purse is kept for it. A record's note says so
   (`base sky gun w16 moved`). The first version of the rule asked whether a sky gun reached **the base** and never fired
   in 72 sample runs: the Flaks of the role spots do reach the base, the Skyray simply rests on the far side of it. The
   rule now measures to the flyer.
3. **The skilled rung's pick is measured, not inherited.** `HeadroomProbeTests.BestRecordedStrategy` first reads
   `Tools/PlayTest/skilled_picks.txt` (`SkilledPicks`), and only for a cell without a line falls back to round 68's
   `plan_records.txt`. The file is written by `Tools/PlayTest/skilled_picks.py --write` from a pressure batch that plays
   every searched strategy of every cell (new policies `strategy1` to `strategy5`) exactly as the skilled rung plays one,
   on seeds 1-3 at the data. Rule: most seeds won, then most base health kept over the seeds, then stars, then the
   lowest number. `plan_records.txt`, `Plans/` and the calibration's inputs are untouched. How to refresh: Docs/COMMANDS.md,
   "Round 78"; a refresh is a new bot stamp by construction.
4. **Not changed, on purpose:** the skilled rung still knows the level (the ledger of the coming waves and the rift a wave
   ahead): it stands for a player who has played the level before. Only the sensible rung is held to what the HUD shows.

  of 360 (Shard Ridge Medium 14, Fault Line Medium 4, Quartz Flats Medium 2, Shard Ridge Psycho 1; Quartz Flats Easy none).

  are lost by attrition, so what is left is more purely the last wave. On Hard it rose (16 -> 25): Quartz Flats Hard is the
  cell (sensible 3 1 1 0 0 -> 3 0 0 0 0, skilled 3 3 1 0 0 -> 3 2 1 0 0). Its runs, old and new, all fall in wave 17, which
  takes 750 to 800 base health in one wave; the version 3 player arrives there with a whole or nearly whole base (its
  Flaks stand in waves 3 and 7 instead of 4 and 10) and loses the same wave. A better player does not
  get through that wave either, so it is the wave, not the bot: round 77's open question 5 stands, sharper.
- **Quartz Flats Medium**: the skilled rung is repaired by its pick (3 3 2 0 0 -> 3 3 3 3 0); the sensible rung gives two
  runs back at the top (3 3 3 3 2 -> 3 3 3 2 1), again in wave 17.

  with a whole base; the tie went to the lower number). One seed is lost at x1.12 and won at x1.25: a fragile run, as the
  critic defined it. A pick measured at the data alone cannot see that; measuring the picks at x1 and x1.12 would
  (question 4).
- Against the targets of the second critic the verdicts stand: Easy all won; Medium sensible 18 of 18 at the data; Hard is
  nowhere easier than Medium; skilled at the data now loses only on Landing Site Psycho (1 of 3) and Quartz Flats Hard

## Round 79: the wave grammar (clusters, breathers, surprises, a boss entrance), measured on all 24 cells; picks refreshed; two cells open (2026-11-17)

Not committed. Two agents: the first built the grammar, solved the waves and measured them (its sections follow as it
wrote them); the second investigated the cells that missed a target, refreshed the skilled rung's picks, ran the gates and
changed no rule and no wave. **Read Docs/WAVE_GRAMMAR.md for the design.** In short: a wave has one front pattern (stream,
spread clusters, swarm, tank escort, combo swarm, air raid) cut into clusters by breathers, may carry one surprise (the
level's rift troops mid-wave, behind the gate where the level has such a rift, or a share down the second road), and a boss
walks in with the last cluster of its wave. One set of numbers per difficulty for every level (`WaveGrammarRules`); a level's
script keeps its roster and its rhythm. Result: Easy 180 of 180 and Medium 178 of 180 runs won, the share of lost runs that
fell in the last wave from a full base 39 % -> 26 %, a won run 8 % longer; the skilled rung wins 22 of 24 cells at the data
with refreshed picks (round 78: 22), Glass Meadows Psycho and Quartz Flats Hard do not. Save MD5
42fbe06b38e133cecfe2014def5c833c after every batch; no `settings.json`.

### What is built (all compiles clean; the stored waves are the grammar's)

- **Grammar code** (`Assets/_Project/Scripts/Balance`): `WavePattern`, `SurpriseKind`, `WaveGrammarRules` (the numbers, one
  object at `BalanceRules.Grammar`), `WaveGrammar` (pattern per wave, which waves carry a surprise), `WaveTimeline` (clusters
  and breathers, active seconds); `WaveComposer.Compose` lays a wave out by them (tank escort, combo swarm, surprise fill,
  boss with the last cluster); `WaveLoad.Span` counts only the seconds something is coming (`PauseCredit` 2 s);
  `WaveSolver.SolveVariant` solves a surprise wave on its own difficulty; `BalanceRules.AmbushFactor` and the rhythm letter
  `M` are gone. `WaveSpec` carries `Pattern`, `Beats`, `Surprise` for reports and tests.
- **Validator:** `Game.Levels.WaveShape.Check`, called by `LevelValidator.CheckWaves` (silence at most 16 s, a wave at most
  120 s, walkers out of one authored nest per wave).
- **Scripts of the first continent** (`LevelSpecs.Crystal.cs`): every `M` is a `P`; Landing Site's rift Cragbacks join in
  wave 7 (was 4, they only ever came in wave 7); new rift troops out of the nest behind the first gate on Glass Meadows
  (Cragback from wave 7, nest 1) and Quartz Flats (Cragback from wave 9, nest 2).
- **Tests:** `Assets/Tests/EditMode/WaveGrammarTests.cs` (22 cases, 21 at the time of the first whole suite; all green in a targeted run on w6 before the last
  four rule changes: no surprise on a swarm, a surprise never empty, rift levels through rifts only, no growth in a
  surprise; **run the class again**). The first whole suite on w6 read 1169 / 1110 passed / 5 failed / 54 skipped. Three

## Round 80b: raids out of the plain mean, the relief bound, the guard gun of a rear rift, scales re-expressed (2026-11-17)

Not committed. One agent, on top of round 80 in the tree. The bot is untouched (`bot=3:f9f8c682` in every record). Save
MD5 42fbe06b38e133cecfe2014def5c833c after every batch; no `settings.json`.

### Decisions recorded (Remco, 2026-11-17, through the coordinator)

- **A surprise may fall on a tank escort wave**: the behaviour as built stays, no rule against it.
- **The Easy purse rule for a rift's flyers is approved** (round 80, rule 2) and so is **the raid cap** (rule 3).
- The coordinator's decisions for this round: raids out of the plain mean in the calibration and in the check, no named
  slack; Fault Line Easy mended by rule or data, not by the test; Glass Meadows Easy's row mended by cause; the guard gun
  in the model's purse before any map change; no bot change.

### What changed, and why

1. **An air raid is no plain wave** (`BalanceChecks.PlainMean`; the mark is `WaveSpec.AirRaid`, stored per wave as
   `WaveDefinition._airRaid` and written by the solve stage). Calibration and gate read the same mean.
2. **That alone did not mend the gate, and the reason is not the one round 80 gave.** With the raids out of the mean
   and round 80's cap as it was, nine cells were still out (Quartz Flats Medium +20.6 %, Fault Line Hard +28 %). The
   softer raids are answered through the purse: the ledger's player buys no further sky gun and has that money on the
   ground. So the cap moved into the one solve: the solver takes a raid's lowest crossing, the trim to the curve never
   lifts a raid above it, and the ground waves are sized for the purse the player then has (`WaveSolver.BisectOn`,
   `CampaignModel.CalibrateToHuman`; `BalanceRules.LowestRaidCrossing` and the second solve are gone).
3. **The relief of "a surprise lifts no wave" is bounded by the curve** (`BalanceRules.SurpriseReliefMost` 0.05). The

### Remco's playtest of the round 80 tree and his decisions (2026-11-17, through the coordinator)

- "The waves feel a lot better": the grammar stays.
- "Sometimes 1 random enemy appears on the road behind a gate; that's not what I meant with surprises." And the design
  that followed, in his words as relayed: all spawn points are the same kind of thing, with a role per level in data
  (main paths, surprise paths); what comes out of a surprise path is configurable per level and per wave (size, creature
  types, pattern; several surprise paths in one wave); a small group, even one big creature, is fine when it is
  authored; what is not fine is a stray creature the composer adds as filler; the grammar may make a default plan by
  rule (spacing and share per difficulty), the level's data overrides it per wave, the solver and ledger budget what is
  configured; any combination of main and surprise paths is allowed in one wave; the threshold stays a data value.
- "Shard Ridge Medium's boss feels quite weak."
- He may place spawn points himself when maps are made or adjusted (none was added this round, see "Not built").

### What changed, and why

1. **The filler is gone** (`WaveComposer.Compose`: "a surprise is never empty" and `AddOne`). That rule, with the Easy
   share buying one heavy troop, made the lone Cragback Remco saw: in the stored waves before this round every surprise of Landing
   Site and Glass Meadows was one Cragback (two as played on Hard and Psycho), and Fault Line Medium wave 7 and Quartz
   Flats Easy wave 10 sent one Shalebat.
2. **The default plan sends a real group or nothing** (`WaveGrammarRules.MinSurpriseGroup` 3, a data value;
   `WaveGrammar.Plan`, `WaveComposer.SurpriseHeads`): the creatures of a default surprise, all its groups together, as
   composed. A wave whose share buys fewer carries none and the next wave that can takes it. The groups may open several
   nests at once (Quartz Flats: bats out of both rifts and a Cragback out of the rear one).
3. **Spawn points have a role in the level's data** (`SpawnRole`; `LevelDefinition._surprisePaths`, `_mainNests`,
   `RoleOfPath`, `RoleOfNest`): a ground path is main unless listed as a surprise path, a nest is a surprise point
   unless listed as a main nest. The defaults are what the six levels are, so no level asset was rewritten.
   `LevelDefinition.IsValid` (and so `OnValidate`) checks the roles.
4. **A level writes its own surprises per wave** (`WaveScriptSpec.Surprises`: `SurpriseSpec`, `SurpriseEntrySpec`;
   helpers `Surprise`, `FromNest`, `DownPath`): creature, number, point, pattern (stream, clusters, swarm), spacing and
   delay per entry; any number of points in one wave; per difficulty range; an entry-less surprise keeps a wave free. A
   written surprise replaces the default on its wave; the front gives up the threat it costs, so the wave is no bigger
   and the kill money stays the script's; the solver and the ledger read the composed groups. `SurpriseSchedule.Check`
   validates a schedule against the level (the solve stage logs `[Validator]` errors; two tests). How a designer sets a
   level's surprises: Docs/WAVE_GRAMMAR.md, "Writing a level's surprises".
5. **Any combination of spawn points in one wave is valid**: the validator's rule "walkers out of at most one authored
   nest per wave" (`WaveShape.WalkerRifts`) is gone.
6. **Landing Site's rear rift is the level's own surprise now** (`LevelSpecs.Crystal`): one Cragback out of the rear
   rift in the middle of wave 7 and once more late (wave 11 on Easy, 10 from Medium on; two as played on Hard and
   Psycho), the waves it had in round 80. That lesson is Remco's (round 31, kept 2026-11-10; Voss's warning hangs on
   it), no wave's share buys three Cragbacks (threat 15 a head; wave 7 has 29), and "one big creature is fine when it is
   authored". **Glass Meadows has no surprise any more**: its rear-rift Cragback was round 79's addition and all filler.
   Question 1 below.
7. **The flank of Shard Ridge was checked against "out of a spawn point"**: it walks in at the start of the second
   road, at that road's route gate, which is an authored spawn point of the level (`LevelVisualBuilder`, the living
   route gate); nothing spawns on a road segment, and a flank's share buys a group on every wave that carries one (the
   group rule holds for it too). Nothing changed. Its role in the data is a main path: see "Not built".
8. **`LevelBossAlone` Medium 0.25 -> 0.3** (the value of rounds 64 to 76; round 77 lowered it for Quartz Flats Medium,
   which has since gone from 2 of 3 to 15 of 15 on both rungs). Shard Ridge Medium's Brood Mother asked 0.21 of the

9. **Seven builder scales refitted** (`ScaleRefit.cs`, `scale_refit_r81.txt`), because a surprise one wave later moves a

## UI fix: level picker hints (2026-11-18)

Remco's screenshot of the region level picker: "Arrow keysleft / right", Q / E glued to their words, the ESC glyph over
"back to the planet", a colon hanging loose, five hints in one line. Not committed.

- **Cause:** the help line (`PromptLine`) was one horizontal layout stretched over a fixed box. The keyboard hint was
  wider than the box, so the layout squeezed every piece below its own width (they then overlap) before the line was
  scaled down; and the gaps were the spaces at the ends of text runs, which a text component does not measure.
- **Fix in the shared helper** (`Scripts/UI/Glyphs/PromptLine.cs`, new `PromptLineLayout.cs` and `PromptPiece.cs`): a
  template is read into rows (`\n`), hint groups (two or more spaces) and pieces (words or a hole); the gaps between a
  glyph and its words, around the slash of a glyph pair, between groups and between rows are fixed sizes of the layout.
  The block takes the size its rows ask for and only then shrinks as a whole, so nothing can be squeezed into its
  neighbour. A hole without a glyph (the keyboard's "Arrow keys") prints its name in the key colour.
- **Texts** (`en.ui_menus.txt`, keys unchanged): no colon behind a glyph; the region hints are two centred rows
  (keyboard: move / play / back, then "Down: buttons" and the click hint; pad: move, then play / back / "Down: buttons");
  the planet hint stays one row. `WorldMapScreen` gives the line a two-row box and lifts the caption 40 units above it.
- **Only user of `PromptLine`** is the planet map (planet and region layer), so no other screen changes.
- **Test:** `PromptLineLayoutTests` (4): rows, groups and pieces of a template; punctuation stays tight to its hole; no
  piece has spaces at its ends or double spaces; the three map hints have at most two rows, four groups a row, 96
  characters a row, and words after a glyph start with a letter after a gap (no hanging colon).
- **Checked:** stills at 1920x1080 and 1280x720 of the region and planet layer with keyboard, Xbox and PlayStation
  glyphs, before and after: `ArtSource/Previews/QA/ui_levelpicker_hints_{before,after}_{keys_region,keys_planet,xbox_region,ps_region,ps_planet}_{1080,720}.png`
  and the editor's own Game view `ui_levelpicker_hints_after_keys_region_gameview.png` (`Tools/PlayTest/ui_map_hints.sh`).
  The off-screen stills draw the words over the globe's bright rim fainter than the game does; the Game view capture is
  the sharp one. EditMode suite on clone w6: 1186 tests, 1132 passed, 0 failed, 54 skipped. Save MD5 7a848003... unchanged.
- **Left as it was:** the wording "Down: buttons"; the letter that happens to sit on the globe's bright rim line reads
  a little weaker (no plate behind the line: tried, looked like a box, taken out).

## Round 83: a monotone model player, every wave to its own target, one measured scalar per cell (2026-11-18)

Not committed. One agent, on HEAD ce56b3d5. The critic's review (Docs/BALANCE_CRITIC_2026-11-18.md) was the brief: the
model was patch-stacking around two properties of its own solver. Both are mended, the patch rules are out, and a
cell's level as played now comes from one automated procedure. Remco's save `progress.json` has MD5
7a848003ed6b1261e4bb58757548727b after every batch. The bot was not touched (no bot file changed).

### What changed, and why

0. **The calibration is re-stamped** (`apply-keep`, twice: at the start and after the boss factor changed the hash):
   `inputs 29b36819 (current)`, factors of 2026-11-15 kept. The plan search no longer skips itself.
1. **The ledger's player is monotone** (`Ledger.PlanOf`, `WaveLoad.Of(..., book)`): it decides its purchase on the wave
   as the preview shows it (creatures and numbers at book health, plus what earlier waves left on the road) and never
   on the trial multiplier. A wave's pressure can then only rise with its creatures' health. One more hole showed up
   under the new test: health carried in by earlier waves was "overkilled" with the wave's own small creatures, so a
   paper wave between carried tanks asked more the weaker it got (`WaveLoad.StreamOverkill` mends it). Tests:
   `Round83Tests.AWavesPressure_NeverFalls_AsItsCreaturesGrowTougher` (every stored wave of the 24 cells, both lenses,
   a tenth to ten times its health) and `AWavesAirPressure_NeverFalls_AsItsFlyersGrowTougher` (every raid).
2. **Every wave is solved to its own target, one pass per difficulty** (`WaveSolver.Solve`; Docs/WAVE_GRAMMAR.md, "The
   solver"). No Medium curve that the others copy, no common factor on a level mean, no second solve. Gone with it:
   `WaveSolver.SolveVariant`, `CampaignModel.CalibrateToHuman`, `SizeBosses`, `CapScale`, the 160-step scan, the calm
   solve. The solve stage takes 2 to 3 seconds (27 before); the ledger lab reads all 24 cells in 2 seconds.
3. **Rules removed** (each with its evidence in WAVE_GRAMMAR.md, "Rules of rounds 80 and 80b that round 83 took out"):
   `RaidsCappedAtHeldGuns` and the 5 % crossing walk (one crossing now), `SurprisesLiftNoWave` and
   `SurpriseReliefMost` (no mean to redistribute; test `WaveGrammarTests.ASurprise_MakesNoOtherWaveTougher` on five
   levels), the raids-out-of-the-mean special case in the calibration (`PlainMean` is a reading aid only), the rear-rift
   guard gun (`RearRiftGuardCells`, `BooksRearGuard`: on paper it moved six waves of Glass Meadows and Quartz Flats by 2
   to 14 %, `wave_ledger_r83_noguard.txt`; the cell's scalar is measured with that gun standing), `ScaleRefit`, the 24
   builder scales, the 6 % curve gate in `BalanceLedgerTests`, `LevelBossAloneMost`, `MaxBossGrowth`,
   `CampaignModel.ReferenceInputFor`. **Kept** (rules about the game): the grammar, `MinSurpriseGroup`, spawn roles and
   schedules, road plans, `FlyersAfterBounties`, the Easy purse rule, `RaidHealthFloor`, the band, the 2.5-times-median gate.
   **One rule added to the solver:** no ground wave above 2.2 times the median of the ground waves before it (three
   band rises in a row took a Crysium Vein Psycho swarm to 2.8 times its median). **Known limit of "a surprise lifts no
   wave":** a swarm lives on the upper edge of its band and follows the waves before it, surprise waves included (their
   creatures are fewer and tougher); the test leaves swarms to the median gate.
4. **Builder scales replaced** by `BalanceRules.DifficultyScale` (one factor per difficulty for every level) times one
   scalar per cell from the closed loop (`Tools/PlayTest/closed_loop.py`; WAVE_GRAMMAR.md, "How to balance a new
   level"). Both are plain factors on creature health, exactly what the probe's multiple is, so a measured break-even
   turns into a scalar without a model. Targets: Easy the weaker rung breaks even at x1.4; Medium the sensible rung at
   x1.18; Hard the sensible rung at x0.95 with the skilled rung at x1.06 at least; Psycho the skilled rung at x1.06.
5. **A level's boss is sized first and alone, against the defence that stands for its whole wave**, so
   `LevelBossAlone` is what the boss asks as stored. Read that way the bosses of round 82 ask about 0.35 / 0.55 / 0.65
   / 0.7 (they were read against a defence bought for the boss alone at 0.2 / 0.33 / 0.4 / 0.45); the factors are now
   0.4 / 0.6 / 0.7 / 0.75. The crowd of a boss wave gives way to its boss (down to the solver's floor where that
   makes the wave fit its cap), the boss comes down only where no crowd does, never under its floor.
6. **No walker leaves a spawn point alone in the default plan** (`WaveComposer.DropLoneWalkers`; test
   `Round83Tests.TheDefaultPlan_SendsNoWalkerAlone_OutOfARift`).
7. **Quartz Flats writes its Hard and Psycho surprises**: one Cragback (two as played) out of the rear rift with two
   bats out of the other in wave 10 (Hard) and wave 12 (Hard and Psycho); none in the tank escort of wave 14.
8. **Paper waves are gone by rule**: a ground wave whose pressure is carried in by earlier waves keeps the lower edge of
   its band (x0.7 of the toughest of the three ground waves before it) instead of falling to the floor. Test
   `Round83Tests.NoStoredGroundWave_IsPaper` (none under 0.4 times its cell's median; the four opening waves and the
   crowd of a boss wave are not judged).
9. Tests adjusted: `BalanceLedgerTests` (the paper's reading of the stored hero cap and of the order of the
   difficulties is a report now, as the paper ramp has been since round 22e: the closed loop sets the level),
   `BalanceModelTests` (the solver's API), `Round61Tests` (the purchase is planned at book health),
   `ContinentFinaleTests` (Easy's boss share is judged by the finale probe where it played, as Hard and Psycho are),
   `WaveGrammarTests` (Quartz Flats writes its own on every difficulty; the surprise test). New: `Round83Tests` (6).
10. Docs: WAVE_GRAMMAR.md (the solver, how to balance a new level, the removed rules), COMMANDS.md ("Round 83").

points mended (the finale stage's armour, the boss floors and the wave's lift, the crowd before the boss), and measured.

### What changed, and why (Remco's playtest of level 1 on Easy, Medium and Hard, 2026-11-18: "plays fun")

1. **Easy and Medium a notch softer, Hard and Psycho as they were** ("Easy and Medium a tad too hard; Hard feels right.
   Not much less, but a bit"). The closed loop's targets: Easy, the weaker rung breaks even at x1.55 at least (was
   x1.4, and the old reading "holds the ladder to x1.25" could not see the difference); Medium, the sensible rung at
   x1.32 (was x1.18); one ladder step each. Hard (sensible x0.95, the better rung x1.06 at least) and Psycho (skilled
   x1.06) unchanged. `closed_loop.py` and `ClosedLoopAcceptanceTests` carry the new targets; Easy and Medium are
   measured on ladders that reach them (`r85_measure.sh`: Easy x1 to x1.76, Medium x0.9 to x1.57). Easy is judged on
   its break-even now (it passed by holding x1.25 before).
2. **Every boss walks in armour** ("they have no armour; that should be standard"): `BalanceRules.BossArmourShare`
   0.25, the armour pool of every boss (level and continent bosses) is at least a quarter of its body, so light fire
   chips it at 0.2 and the Cannon and rockets strip it, exactly as on every plated creature (COMBAT_RULES section 1).
   Written into the creature data by the generator (`ProjectGenerator.ArmourOf`), by `BalanceStages.ApplyBossArmour`
   (`ApplyRound85.cs`, menu `Tools/Generate/Balance/12`) and kept by the finale stage when it moves a continent
   boss's health (the pool now moves with the body: the first version kept the pool of the old, bigger body, which
   left Rotbloom with 6800 armour on 17950 body). Kill money follows the formula where the boss was on it.
3. **A boss is three times the toughest ordinary creature before it** ("the lava rocks seem stronger; bosses must
   feel bizarre"). The "lava rocks" are the Cragback, the stone heavy of level 1 (60 body and 160 armour in the book,
   so under light fire it is worth 860 against the 220 of its bar). On Landing Site Easy the boss had the bar of a
   Cragback (392 against 378) and no armour: under light fire a third of one. `BalanceRules.BossOverRegular` 3 on every
   difficulty: a level boss's floor is three times the health bar (body plus armour, as it walks in) of the toughest
   ordinary creature the player met in the level before it. The solver (`WaveSolver.Solve`) sizes the boss first; a
   boss wave over its cap gives way in its crowd first (to the lower edge of its band; with the crowd on its floor, as the first agent had it, a row of Gun Turrets won Landing Site Easy without the Cannon, which the grace gate refuses), then a boss above its floor comes down
   towards it, never under it. A boss on that floor that is over the cap on its own is the wave's fight by rule. Both
   boss floors are taken off the wave's lift now (a capped troop makes every creature of the wave tougher, the boss
   included), so the boss's bar is the floor as it walks in. Under light fire the boss is now 1.4 times a Cragback
   (shells: 3 times); see the question below.
4. **The laser's free kills** ("bizarrely strong on Easy and Medium, on Psycho actually not"). Cause, with numbers
   (`Tools/PlayTest/laser_share.txt`, `LaserDuel.Difficulties`): a beam holds one creature and swings on the moment it
   dies; every kill cost it only the sweep time (0.05 s) instead of the rest of its pulse. A creature that dies in one or
   two pulses then dies up to four times as fast as the laser's data says. Skitters, the swarm of level 1, spawn with
   12 health on Easy, 22 on Medium and Hard and 51 on Psycho: one or two pulses on Easy, seven on Psycho. So the same
   tower was worth more the lower a difficulty's health. One rule (`IHitBudget`, `Tower.ReleaseBeam`): the pulse that
   kills costs the beam the share of it the creature needed; a beam wastes nothing on a dead body and gains nothing
   either. Its role (light fire that wastes nothing on a swarm) is kept.

5. **Throttle tools** (Remco uses the PC while batches run): `Tools/PlayTest/lower_priority.sh` (+ `.ps1`) puts every
   worker and stage Unity process at BelowNormal right after a launch (`pressure.sh`, `workers.sh`,
   `finale_workers.sh`, `r34b_editmode_worker.sh`, `stage.sh start`); the clones' product-name line is matched as
   `Tower defense.*`, so a clone of the stage gets its worker name. `closed_loop.py` reads a one-seed pass
   (`PR_SEEDS=1`: a multiple is held with that seed). New reading tools: `boss_vs_regular.py` (with the column "boss
   over the toughest creature before it"), `ledger_bosses.py`, `tower_mix.py`, `LaserDuel.Difficulties`.

### The closed loop (four measurements and a targeted one)

- **M1, one seed** (`pressure_r85_m1_*`, 252 runs on two clones at BelowNormal, 43 minutes): written with
  `--step 1.12` (one ladder step at most, the pass being coarse), Easy never toughened (Crysium Vein Easy kept),
  Quartz Flats Hard on its bound 0.7. The Medium scalars before it came from round 84's reading against the new
  target (x0.896; five of six landed on x1.32 at once).
- **M2, three seeds** (`pressure_r85_final2_*`, 756 runs on five clones, 63 minutes): Fault Line Medium (x1.06) and
  Hard (x1.18), Landing Site Hard (x1.18) and Psycho (x0.85), Glass Meadows Psycho (over x1.32) and Crysium Vein Psycho
  read two steps off: bisected between M1 and M2 (round 84's rule). Hard folded: `DifficultyScale` Hard 0.993 ->
  0.913 (the geometric mean of its six scalars), the scalars divided by the same, so Quartz Flats Hard could go 8 %
  under its old bound. Landing Site Easy's weaker rung was the skilled pick, which broke at the armoured boss from
  x1.25 on (all Pulse Rifles): see the bot batch.
- **Bot batch, one cell** (`skilled_picks_r85_ls_easy_records.txt`, its own stamp): Landing Site Easy searched anew on
  the round 85 data, three fresh strategies plus the old pick played on the Easy ladder; the fresh strategy2 holds
  x1 to x1.76 and is the pick (written by hand in `skilled_picks.txt` with a comment; the other 23 picks are round
  83b's).
- **M3** (`pressure_r85_final3_*`, 756 runs, data 66f9d292): 24 of 24 within a step. But on that data a row of Gun
  Turrets won Landing Site Easy without the Cannon (the grace gate broke): the crowd of a boss wave over its cap stood
  on its floor. The solver was changed (the crowd gives way to the lower edge of its band, no further) and
- **M4** (`pressure_r85_final4_*`) measured that: the boss waves had grown (Glass Meadows Psycho wave 9 and 12 carried
  2.7 times the crowd), Glass Meadows Psycho read under x0.75 (every loss in wave 12), Landing Site Psycho x0.85,
  Glass Meadows Hard x0.85 (better rung under its guard), Glass Meadows Easy x1.32.
- **The last pass** (third agent). Scalars from M4's break-evens: Landing Site Psycho 1.133 -> 0.87, Glass Meadows
  Easy 0.921 -> 0.81, Hard 1.196 -> 0.97, Psycho 1.132 -> 0.94, Fault Line Medium 1.02 -> 0.9 (it read x1.18 on two
  scalars: the one Medium cell that had not had its notch). **A solver mend came with it** (`WaveSolver.Solve`): on
  Glass Meadows Psycho every scalar under 0.96 failed `BalanceLedgerTests.EveryWave_StaysInsideItsDifficultyBand`
  (wave 10, the plain wave after the wave 9 boss, pressure 3.31 over its band 2.63). Cause, read on the paper lab
  (`WaveLedgerLab` at fifteen scalars from 0.7 to 1.08): a plain wave that the boss before it holds over the hero cap
  stayed on the lower edge of its band when even its least crowd missed the cap, and dropped to the cap when it just
  met it: wave 10 stood x1.58 at scalar 0.96 and x2.65 at 0.94, 1.7 times tougher for a softer cell. Now such a wave
  gives way to its share of the median (`LeastOfMedian`, no paper crowd). It moved Glass Meadows Psycho wave 10 and
  Fault Line Hard waves 7, 9 and 10, nothing else (ledger compared wave by wave). A targeted measurement of the six
  moved cells (`pressure_r85_t1_*`, 20 minutes) read all six inside a step before the full chain was spent.
- **Final** (`pressure_r85_final5_*`, 756 runs on five clones; Easy 16 min, Medium 17 min, Hard and Psycho 28 min).

The game keeps no damage per tower, so the share of a Gun+Laser pair (weighted by the health of the level's ground
creatures, where the Cragback dominates) is the closest reading; it does not move, because the fault lived on small
bodies only. Per coin against the swarm the laser was 29 % better than the gun on Easy and 7 % on Psycho; now 14 and
7 % at level 1. What is left of the spread is pulse quantisation (a creature that needs 1.2 pulses wastes 0.8 of the
second on any gun). The bot rungs barely build the laser (tower levels bought at the data, round 84 -> 85: Easy 1 %
-> 0 %, Medium 0 % -> 0 %, Hard 1 % -> 1 %, Psycho 11 % -> 10 %), so the measurement says nothing about it; Remco's
play does.
